STUDYQURAN:5:27/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r1.claim: The Cain and Abel account parallels Genesis and presents fallen humanity's tendency toward violence against its own brothers.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r1.anchor: like its Biblical version the Quranic story of Cain and Abel serves as a prototype of the inclination of fallen human beings toward violence

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r2.claim: Some commentators read the story in its sūrah context as a subtle commentary on issues concerning the People of the Book.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r2.anchor: the story is read by some commentators as offering a subtle commentary on issues related particularly to the People of the Book

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r3.claim: The command to recite truthfully may address Jews and/or idolaters who plotted to kill Muhammad and some Companions.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r3.anchor: Recite unto them, with truth may mean that Muhammad should relate this account to the Jews and/or the idolaters

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r4.claim: The idiom for stretching hands against someone links the plot against Muhammad in 5:11 with Cain's intent to kill Abel.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r4.anchor: The idiomatic phrase stretch forth their hands against is also used to describe the intent to kill in the present account

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r5.claim: The story may target Jews and Christians whose hostility to Muhammad's message arose from spiritual envy; envy among earlier religious communities is noted elsewhere.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r5.anchor: it may be directed at those Jews and Christians who were hostile to Muhammad’s message out of spiritual envy

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r7.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the story encourages Muslims to treat the Jews who plotted against Muhammad and his followers leniently, following Abel's restraint.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r7.anchor: Al-Ṭabarī, however, suggests that the reason for telling this story was to encourage the Muslims to deal leniently

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites a hadith telling Muslims to follow the better of Adam's two sons and leave the worse path.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r8.anchor: Verily God gives you the example of the two sons of Adam; so take [the path of] the better of the two

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r9.claim: Adam's two sons are the Biblical Cain, Qābīl, and Abel, Hābīl.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r9.anchor: Adam’s two sons refers to the Biblical Cain (Qābīl) and Abel (Hābīl).

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r10.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r10.claim: One account says God commanded the brothers to sacrifice; another says they competed for the right to marry Cain's twin sister, whom both desired.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r10.anchor: The two were either commanded by God to offer a sacrifice (Ṭ) or, according to some commentators, engaged in rival sacrifices

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r11.claim: Herdsman Abel offered a fattened sheep while crop-grower Cain offered produce.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r11.anchor: Abel, being a herdsman, offered a fattened sheep for the sacrifice, while Cain, who grew crops, offered some of his produce.

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r12.claim: The Qur'an, like Genesis, identifies the accepted and rejected offerings but does not state why God chose one.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r12.anchor: but, like the Biblical account, does not indicate the reason for this choice.

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r13.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r13.claim: Some say Abel offered his prized sheep while Cain offered the poorest of his crops, explaining rejection of Cain's sacrifice.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r13.anchor: Some commentators explain that while Abel sacrificed his most prized sheep, Cain offered the poorest produce from his crop

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r14.claim: Qurbān derives from a root associated with nearness, so sacrifice is understood chiefly as a means of drawing near to God.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r14.anchor: Sacrifice here renders qurbān, a word whose root, q-r-b, is related primarily to nearness

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r15.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r15.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says both brothers primarily sought closeness to God, casting doubt on reports that their offerings competed for a woman.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r15.anchor: Al-Ṭabarī notes that closeness to God was the essential motivation of both Cain and Abel

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r16.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r16.claim: Al-Rāzī attributes pious intent in the sacrifice only to Abel.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r16.anchor: al-Rāzī attributes pious intent in the sacrifice only to Abel.

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r17.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r17.claim: Abel implies Cain's offering was rejected because it lacked reverence or fear of God and was lowly and unfitting.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r17.anchor: the latter’s sacrifice was not accepted because it had not been done with proper “reverence” or fear of God

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r18.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r18.claim: For earlier communities sacrifice was analogous to Muslim charity; prayer, fasting, righteous acts, and obligatory alms take its place in Islam.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r18.anchor: Al-Ṭabarī notes that the practice of sacrificial offering for earlier religious communities was like the practices of charity and alms for Muslims

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r19.claim: The verb qarraba used for offering sacrifice can also describe giving charity.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r19.anchor: Offered a sacrifice translates qarraba, a verb that can also be used in connection with giving charity

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r20.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r20.claim: Because prayer, fasting, and charity parallel sacrifice, the verse broadly teaches that God accepts ritual and moral acts only when performed with reverence.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r20.anchor: only ritual or moral acts done with “reverence” are accepted by God

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r21.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r21.claim: Pilgrimage sacrifice and ʿĪd al-aḍḥā commemorate God's stopping Abraham's test and providing a ram; the meat is distributed as charity.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r21.anchor: both of which commemorate God’s halting Abraham’s test, during which he was to sacrifice his son

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r22.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r22.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r22.claim: The teaching that neither sacrificial flesh nor blood reaches God, but reverence does, partly supports al-Ṭabarī's charity analogy.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r22.anchor: Neither their flesh nor their blood will reach God, but the reverence from you reaches Him

TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r1.claim: Muhammad is to recount the story to Jews who planned violence against him and his companions, warning them through the outcomes of injustice, treachery, and broken covenants: the faithful son was rewarded and the oathbreaker punished.
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r1.anchor: واتل على هؤلاء اليهود الذين هموا أن يبسطوا أيديهم إليكم، عليك وعلى أصحابك معك، وعرفهم مكروه عاقبة الظلم والمكر،

TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r2.claim: One view says God commanded Adam's sons to offer sacrifices; the accepted offering came from the son who gave the best of his property, while the other gave its worst. They were Habil and Qabil, Adam's sons.
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r2.anchor: فقال بعضهم: كان ذلك عن أمر الله جل وعز إياهما بتقريبه. وكان سبب القبول أن المتقبل منه قرب خير ماله

TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r3.speaker: إسماعيل بن رافع
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r3.claim: Ismail ibn Rafi reports that the shepherd offered a beloved lamb, which God accepted; it continued grazing in Paradise until it was offered as ransom for Abraham's son.
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r3.anchor: عن هشام بن سعيد، عن إسماعيل بن رافع، قال: بلغني أن ابني آدم لما أمرا بالقربان، كان أحدهما صاحب غنم،

TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r4.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says the shepherd offered his fattest, best sheep willingly, while the farmer grudgingly offered poor grain; God accepted the sheep, and the murdered brother was stronger but piety kept him from striking his brother.
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، قال: إن ابني آدم اللذين قربا قربانا

TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r5.claim: A contrary view says the sacrifice was not offered at God's command to the two brothers.
TAB-FULL:v8p316#2/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: لم يكن ذلك من أمرهما عن أمر الله إياهما به

TAB-FULL:v8p321/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p321/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p321/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says offerings were made because there were no poor people to receive charity; God accepted an offering by sending fire to consume it, while rejected offerings were left untouched. A shepherd offered his best sheep, a farmer his least-liked grain, and the rejected son threatened his brother out of shame; his brother answered that God accepts only from the pious.
TAB-FULL:v8p321/r1.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس، قال: كان من شأنهما أنه لم يكن مسكين فيتصدق عليه،

TAB-FULL:v8p321/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p321/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v8p321/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the brothers as Adam's biological sons Habil and Qabil: one offered a sheep and the other vegetables or crops; the fire accepted the sheep, and the rejected brother killed its owner.
TAB-FULL:v8p321/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد

TAB-FULL:v8p321/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p321/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v8p321/r3.claim: A report heard from Mujahid says God bound one of Cain's legs to his thigh for life, turned his face toward the sun, and placed him under alternating winter shelters of ice and summer shelters of fire, attended by seven angels in succession.
TAB-FULL:v8p321/r3.anchor: قال: ثنا رجل، سمع مجاهدا، في قوله: {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق إذ قربا قربانا}

TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that one brother offered a ram and the other a heap of food; God accepted the offering of the sheep's owner. Another report from him simply identifies them as two Adamites, one accepted and one rejected.
TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس: {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق إذ قربا قربانا فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر} [المائدة: 27] قال: " قرب هذا كبشا وقرب هذا صبرة من طعام؛

TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r2.speaker: عطية
TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r2.claim: Atiyya says Qabil was a farmer and Habil a shepherd; one offered a choice lamb and the other inferior crops, so the fire consumed the lamb and Qabil threatened his brother.
TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r2.anchor: عن فضيل بن مرزوق، عن عطية: {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق} [المائدة: 27] قال: " كان أحدهما اسمه قابيل والآخر هابيل؛

TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق عن بعض أهل العلم بالكتاب الأول
TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r3.claim: A report from earlier-scripture scholars says Adam arranged cross-marriages between the twins; Habil accepted, but Qabil refused, claiming superiority and wanting his own twin sister. Some said Qabil's twin was especially beautiful and he coveted her. Adam settled the dispute by offering whichever son had his sacrifice accepted the right to marry the girl; Habil brought a prime lamb and Qabil grain (some say a cow), and a white fire consumed Habil's offering alone.
TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، عن بعض أهل العلم بالكتاب الأول: " أن آدم أمر ابنه قابيل أن ينكح أخته توأمة هابيل،

TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p321#2/r4.claim: Al-Tabari leaves uncertain which of the reported explanations for the brothers' marriage dispute was true.

TAB-FULL:v8p323/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p323/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v8p323/r1.claim: Al-Suddi reports, through Abu Malik and Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas, Murrah from Ibn Masud, and other Companions, that each birth brought paired twins; Habil wanted Qabil's prettier twin, but Qabil refused. Adam left for Mecca after asking the heavens, earth, and mountains to guard the family; only Qabil agreed. Habil offered a fat young ewe while Qabil gave a bundle of grain after eating its best seed, and fire accepted Habil's offering, prompting Qabil's threat.
TAB-FULL:v8p323/r1.anchor: عن السدي، فيما ذكر عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس، من أصحاب النبي

TAB-FULL:v8p323/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p323/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v8p323/r2.claim: Qatada says Habil offered the best of his flock and fire consumed it, while Qabil offered inferior crops and the fire did not descend; accepted offerings were consumed by fire, but rejected ones were eaten by birds and beasts, leading Qabil to envy and threaten his brother.
TAB-FULL:v8p323/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق} [المائدة: 27] ذكر لنا أنهما هابيل وقابيل.

TAB-FULL:v8p324/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p324/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v8p324/r1.claim: Qatada identifies the brothers as Cain and Abel: one farmed and one herded; Abel offered his best, the other his worst, and envy led the rejected brother to threaten murder.
TAB-FULL:v8p324/r1.anchor: قتادة في قوله: {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق} [المائدة: 27] قال: " هما قابيل وهابيل

TAB-FULL:v8p324/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p324/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v8p324/r2.claim: Mujahid says one offered grain and the other a ewe; fire left the grain and consumed the ewe.
TAB-FULL:v8p324/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد : {إذ قربا قربانا} [المائدة: 27] قال: «قرب هذا زرعا وذا عناقا، فتركت النار الزرع وأكلت العناق

TAB-FULL:v8p324/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p324/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v8p324/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says the two men were Israelites, not Adam’s direct sons; offerings were practiced among the Israelites, and Adam was the first to die.
TAB-FULL:v8p324/r3.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: كان الرجلان اللذان في القرآن، اللذان قال الله: {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق} [المائدة: 27] من بني إسرائيل

TAB-FULL:v8p324/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p324/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p324/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that they were Adam’s direct sons: the audience knew offerings belonged to Adam’s descendants, so the account would add nothing if it concerned distant Israelite descendants; reports and exegetes likewise place them in Adam’s lifetime.
TAB-FULL:v8p324/r4.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك عندي بالصواب، أن اللذين قربا القربان كان ابني آدم لصلبه , لا من ذريته من بني إسرائيل

TAB-FULL:v8p326/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r1.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r1.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd reports that Adam grieved without laughing for a hundred years after his son killed his brother; he was then greeted with a wish that God make him laugh.
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r1.anchor: عن سالم بن أبي الجعد، قال: " لما قتل ابن آدم أخاه

TAB-FULL:v8p326/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r2.claim: Ali reports Adam’s lament after Abel’s murder, with verses mourning the altered land and a reply lamenting Abel’s death and the living as a slaughtered corpse.
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r2.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق الهمداني، قال: قال علي بن أبي طالب رضوان الله عليه: لما قتل ابن آدم أخاه، بكى آدم فقال

TAB-FULL:v8p326/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r3.claim: The text does not establish whether God commanded the brothers to offer; either is possible, but either way they offered in an attempt to draw near to God.
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r3.anchor: وجائز أن يكون كان عن أمر الله إياهما بذلك، وجائز أن يكون عن غير أمره. غير أنه أي ذلك كان فلم يقربا ذلك إلا طلب قربة إلى الله

TAB-FULL:v8p326/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r4.claim: The rejected offerer tells the one whose offering was accepted, “I will kill you.”
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r4.anchor: وأما تأويل قوله: {قال لأقتلنك} [المائدة: 27] فإن معناه: قال الذي لم يتقبل منه قربانه للذي تقبل منه قربانه

TAB-FULL:v8p326/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r5.claim: The wording omits the identities of the accepted and rejected offerers because the preceding mention of both makes repeating them unnecessary.
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r5.anchor: فترك ذكر المتقبل قربانه والمردود عليه قربانه , استغناء بما قد جرى من ذكرهما عن إعادته

TAB-FULL:v8p326/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that the brother answered that the rejection was not his fault: God accepts only from the God-fearing.
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {قال لأقتلنك} [المائدة: 27] فقال له أخوه: ما ذنبي {إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين}

TAB-FULL:v8p326/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the rejected brother’s offering was adulterated with the worst he had, while the other offered his best; had he feared God in his offering, it would have been accepted.
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين} [المائدة: 27] قال: " يقول: إنك لو اتقيت الله في قربانك تقبل منك، جئت بقربان مغشوش بأشر ما عندك

TAB-FULL:v8p326/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r8.claim: The God-fearing are those who fear God by carrying out required duties and avoiding what He forbids.
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r8.anchor: ويعني بقوله: {من المتقين} [المائدة: 27] من الذين اتقوا الله وخافوه بأداء ما كلفهم من فرائضه واجتناب ما نهاهم عنه من معصيته

TAB-FULL:v8p326/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r9.speaker: جماعة من أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r9.claim: Some exegetes interpret the God-fearing here as those who avoid associating partners with God.
TAB-FULL:v8p326/r9.anchor: وقد قال جماعة من أهل التأويل: المتقون في هذا الموضع الذين اتقوا الشرك

TAB-FULL:v8p327/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the God-fearing in this verse are those who avoid shirk.
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك، قوله: {إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين} [المائدة: 27] الذين يتقون الشرك

TAB-FULL:v8p327/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r2.claim: Qurbān is the verbal noun on the pattern of furqān from faraqa and ʿudwān from ʿadā.
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r2.anchor: وقد بينا معنى القربان فيما مضى، وأنه الفعلان من قول القائل: قرب، كما الفرقان: الفعلان من فرق، والعدوان من عدا

TAB-FULL:v8p327/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r3.claim: Offerings among earlier peoples were like charity and zakat; acceptance was shown when fire consumed an offering. In the Muslim community, offerings are righteous deeds, with no immediate way to know which are accepted.
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r3.anchor: وكانت قرابين الأمم الماضية قبل أمتنا كالصدقات والزكوات فينا، غير أن قرابينهم كان يعلم المتقبل منها وغير المتقبل فيما ذكر بأكل النار ما تقبل منها وترك النار ما لم يتقبل منها

TAB-FULL:v8p327/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r4.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله العنبري
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r4.claim: At death, ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAnbarī wept because he heard God say that He accepts only from the God-fearing.
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r4.anchor: عن عامر بن عبد الله العنبري، أنه حين حضرته الوفاة بكى، فقيل له: ما يبكيك

TAB-FULL:v8p327/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r5.claim: Some say the offering of the God-fearing is prayer.
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r5.anchor: وقد قال بعضهم: قربان المتقين: الصلاة

TAB-FULL:v8p327/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r6.speaker: عدي بن ثابت
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r6.claim: ʿAdī ibn Thābit says prayer was the offering of the God-fearing.
TAB-FULL:v8p327/r6.anchor: عن عدي بن ثابت، قال: " كان قربان المتقين: الصلاة "

TABATABAI:5:27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27/r1.claim: The story connects to the preceding address to the People of Israel: their rejection of Muhammad arose from envy and transgression, like the envy that drives one brother to murder and futile regret; the lesson is to abandon envy and disbelief.
TABATABAI:5:27/r1.anchor: فإن إباءهم عن قبول الدعوة الحقة لم يكن إلا حسدا وبغيا، وهذا شأن الحسد

TABATABAI:5:27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27/r2.claim: Tilawa is reading, named for following one part of the report after another; naba is news of consequence and benefit; qurban is what one uses to draw near to God or another, originally a verbal noun; taqabbul is acceptance with added care.

TABATABAI:5:27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27/r3.claim: The pronoun “them” addresses the People of the Book, who have been the intended audience in the preceding discourse.
TABATABAI:5:27/r3.anchor: والضمير في قوله { عليهم } لأهل الكتاب لما مر

TABATABAI:5:27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27/r4.claim: The Adam meant here is the Adam the Qur'an identifies as the father of humankind.
TABATABAI:5:27/r4.anchor: والمراد بهذا المسمى بآدم هو آدم الذي يذكر القرآن أنه أبو البشر

TABATABAI:5:27/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:5:27/r5.claim: Some exegetes say Adam was an Israelite man, not the first human, whose sons disputed their offerings; Qabil or Qayin then killed Habil.
TABATABAI:5:27/r5.anchor: وقد ذكر بعض المفسرين أنه كان رجلا من بني إسرائيل تنازع ابناه في قربان قرباه

TABATABAI:5:27/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27/r6.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects that account: the Qur'an uses Adam for the father of humankind, and an alternate Adam would need an identifying clue to prevent ambiguity.
TABATABAI:5:27/r6.anchor: وهو فاسد أما أولا فلأن القرآن لم يذكر ممن سمي بآدم

TABATABAI:5:27/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27/r7.claim: The crow episode suits the primitive intellectual simplicity of the first human, who did not know that the dead could be covered in earth; it is implausible for a member of Israelite society and civilization.
TABATABAI:5:27/r7.anchor: فالآية ظاهرة في أن القاتل ما كان يدري أن الميت يمكن أن يستر جسده بمواراته في الأرض

TABATABAI:5:27-32/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r1.claim: The dialogue and context show both brothers knew whose offering was accepted, though the verse does not say how they learned it.
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r1.anchor: وسياق الكلام يدل على أنهما علما تقبل قربان أحدهما وعدم تقبله من الآخر

TABATABAI:5:27-32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r2.claim: Earlier peoples, or Israelites in particular, apparently recognized acceptance when fire consumed an offering; 3:183 mentions this custom, plausibly also used here before a People of the Book audience.
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r2.anchor: غير أنه ذكر في موضع من كلامه تعالى أنه كان من المعهود عند الأمم السابقة

TABATABAI:5:27-32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r3.claim: The killer is the brother whose offering was rejected; envy alone explains his threat, since the victim committed no voluntary offense that could warrant it.
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r3.anchor: هو الذي لم يتقبل قربانه، وأنه إنما قال ذلك حسدا من نفسه

TABATABAI:5:27-32/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r4.claim: The victim says acceptance is God's decision, not his own, and the killer is at fault for lacking piety; the victim will not kill his brother because he fears God and will not choose injustice and Hell.
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r4.anchor: وإنما الاجرام من قبل القاتل حيث لم يتق الله فجازاه الله بعدم قبول قربانه

TABATABAI:5:27-32/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r5.claim: The restriction may be a restriction of individuals, excluding acceptance of both pious and impious offerings, or a restriction of reversal, correcting the killer's belief that his offering would be accepted over the victim's.
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r5.anchor: مسوق لقصر الأفراد للدلالة على أن التقبل لا يشمل قربان التقي وغير التقي جميعا

TABATABAI:5:27-32/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r6.claim: The story teaches that acceptance of worship depends on piety and warns against murder, injustice, and envy; divine recompense follows a just cosmic order that deters the wrongdoer or assigns him the Fire he merits.
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r6.anchor: وفي الكلام بيان لحقيقة الأمر في تقبل العبادات والقرابين، وموعظة وبلاغ في أمر القتل والظلم والحسد

TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r6.claim: The slain brother is shown to be pious by his statement that God accepts only the pious, which God repeats without correction, and knowledgeable of God by his professed fear of Him, likewise affirmed.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r6.anchor: المتضمن لدعوى التقوى، وقد أمضاها الله تعالى بنقله من غير رد

TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r2.claim: The warning lays out religion’s foundations: one Lord governs all, people divide into pious and unjust, God loves justice and hates oppression, worship requires piety, wrongdoing incurs liability, and the afterlife repays wrongdoers with hell.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r2.anchor: أصول المعارف الدينية ومجامع علوم المبدأ والمعاد أفاضها هذا العبد الصالح إفاضة ضافية

TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r1.claim: Human creation entails innate true cognition, including monotheism; deviations misuse innate faculties rather than abolish their built-in orientation.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r1.anchor: فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها

TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r2.claim: The claim that pure rational inquiry is unreliable because it often errs relies on rational premises and so cannot coherently refute reason; error reflects misuse of reason.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r2.anchor: الأبحاث العقلية المحضة، والقياسات المؤلفة من مقدمات بعيدة من الحس يكثر وقوع الخطأ فيها

TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r3.claim: Empirical arguments for trusting sense and experiment also depend on rational premises, so they cannot use reason to cancel reliance on reason.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r3.anchor: والدليلان كما ترى سيقا لإثبات وجوب الاعتماد على الحس والتجربة

TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r4.claim: Experiments, analogy, and personal approval cannot establish revealed laws; broad moral principles are innate, while their detailed prescriptions must come through revelation.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#13/r4.anchor: والقرآن يبطل ذلك كله بإثبات أن الأحكام المشرعة فطرية بينة

TABATABAI:5:27-32#14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#14/r1.claim: The Qur'an forbids following what one does not know or Satan's steps, and calls the revealed law truth; speculation cannot replace it.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#14/r1.anchor: ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم

TABATABAI:5:27-32#14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#14/r2.claim: Since what lies beyond truth is error and God does not guide the astray, false or unjust means cannot yield truth, justice, goodness, or piety.

TABATABAI:5:27-32#14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#14/r3.claim: The Qur'an bars reflection detached from piety; it pairs legal instruction with moral virtues that awaken piety and help people understand the ruling.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#14/r3.anchor: يحظر على الناس التفكر من غير مصاحبة تقوى الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r1.claim: A report from Abu Jaʿfar says envy led Qabil to stalk and kill Habil secretly; its longer account also treats Adam's later succession and the prophets' legacy.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r1.anchor: عن حبيب السجستاني، عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال لما قرب ابنا آدم القربان

TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r1.claim: Narrations call the brothers Habil and Qabil, while the circulating Torah has Habil and Qayin; the Torah naming has no evidentiary force because its chain ends with an unknown person and its text is altered.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r1.anchor: اسم الابنين هابيل وقابيل، والذي في التوراة الدائرة هابيل وقايين

TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r2.speaker: علي بن الحسين
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r2.claim: In a report from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, Habil offered a prized ram and Qabil a sheaf; Satan taught Qabil to smash Habil's head with stones, and a raven taught him burial, after which Adam mourned and received Hibat Allah (Shith).
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r2.anchor: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام يحدث رجالا من قريش قال لما قربا ابنا آدم القربان

TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r4.claim: Other reports transmitted by Sunni and Shiʿi routes have content close to the al-Qummi account.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r4.anchor: وهناك روايات أخر مروية من طرق أهل السنة والشيعة يقرب مضمونها من مضمون هذه الرواية

TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r1.speaker: روايات
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r1.claim: One report says God kept Habil's ram in Paradise for forty years before it became the ram sacrificed by Abraham in place of Ishmael.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r1.anchor: إن الله أخذ كبش هابيل فخزنه في الجنة اربعين خريفا

TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r9.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects these and similar reports as mostly or entirely weak, inconsistent with sound reflection and the Qur'an, and likely fabricated, distorted, or corrupted in transmission.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r9.anchor: فهذه وأمثالها روايات من طرق جلها أو كلها ضعيفة

TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r2.speaker: التوراة
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r2.claim: Genesis 4 presents Cain and Abel's offerings, Cain's murder of his brother, the curse and mark placed on Cain, and his departure to Nod.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r2.anchor: فقال الرب لقايين أين هابيل أخوك؟ فقال لا أعلم أحارس أنا لأخي

TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r3.claim: Al-Tabataba'i urges readers to compare the Torah's account of the brothers with the Qur'an's account and judge the differences.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r3.anchor: وعليك أن تتدبر ما تشتمل عليه القصة على ما قصتها التوراة وعلى ما قصها القرآن

TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r1.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says the Torah portrays God anthropomorphically as an earthly human who approaches, speaks to, withdraws from, and hides from people; God is exalted above this.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r1.anchor: فأول ما يبدو لك من التوراة انها جعلت الرب تعالى موجودا أرضيا على صورة إنسان

TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r2.claim: That portrayal implies humans once lived face to face with God and that God later hid from Cain, contradicting human sameness and God's transcendence of material conditions.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r2.anchor: مع أن البراهين القاطعة قائمة على أن الإنسان نوع واحد متماثل الأفراد

TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r3.claim: The Qur'an assumes humans are alike and uses the raven's burial of another raven to show humanity's gradual development through sensory and intellectual learning.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r3.anchor: وأما القرآن فإنه يقص القصة على أساس تماثل الأفراد غير أنه يذيل قصة القتل بقصة بعث الغراب

TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r4.claim: Habil's dialogue conveys innate religious knowledge: monotheism, prophethood, resurrection, piety, injustice, divine law, and God's justice in acceptance and afterlife recompense.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r4.anchor: ثم يذكر محاورة الأخوين فيقص عن المقتول من غرر المعارف الفطرية الإنسانية وأصول المعارف الدينية

TABRISI:5:27/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:27/r1.claim: Qurbān is a righteous deed intended to draw near to God's mercy; it follows the faʿlān pattern from qurb, like furqān, shukrān, and kufrān, and royal courtiers are qarābīn because of their closeness.
TABRISI:5:27/r1.anchor: القربان ما يقصد به القرب من رحمة الله من أعمال البر

TABRISI:5:27/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:27/r2.claim: Idh is attached to nabāʾ: the report concerns what happened when both offered, with a singular qurbān because each offered one.
TABRISI:5:27/r2.anchor: إذ قربا متعلق بقوله: { نبأ } والتقدير

TABRISI:5:27/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:5:27/r3.claim: An alternative treats qurbān as a generic noun, usable for one or several offerings, or as a verbal noun of qarraba.
TABRISI:5:27/r3.anchor: القربان اسم جنس فهو يصلح للواحد والمتعدد

TABRISI:5:27/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:27/r4.claim: Muḥammad is told to recite truthfully to his audience the account of Adam's two sons.
TABRISI:5:27/r4.anchor: واتل } أي واقرأ { عليهم } يا محمد

TABRISI:5:27/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27/r5.speaker: أجمعوا، الحسن
TABRISI:5:27/r5.claim: All authorities agree they were Adam's biological sons, except al-Ḥasan, who says they were two men from the Children of Israel.
TABRISI:5:27/r5.anchor: وأجمعوا على أنهما كانا ابني آدم لصلبه إلا الحسن

TABRISI:5:27/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:27/r6.claim: Accepting an act of obedience means making its reward obligatory.

TABRISI:5:27/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27/r7.speaker: قالوا
TABRISI:5:27/r7.claim: They say acceptance in that era was marked by fire descending to consume the accepted offering but not the rejected one.
TABRISI:5:27/r7.anchor: وكانت علامة القبول في ذلك الزمان نارا تأتي

TABRISI:5:27/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:5:27/r8.claim: Mujāhid gives the opposite sign: fire consumed the rejected offering; the author says the first account is more apparent.
TABRISI:5:27/r8.anchor: كانت النار تأكل المردود عن مجاهد والأول أظهر

TABRISI:5:27/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:27/r9.claim: The one whose offering was not accepted threatened the accepted brother with murder; the dialogue fills in the reason for the threat and the response.
TABRISI:5:27/r9.anchor: التقدير قال الذي لم يتقبل منه للذي تقبل منه لأقتلنك

TABRISI:5:27/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:27/r10.claim: God accepts only from those who avoid sins; the omitted qualification is understood because this is what one should fear most.

TABRISI:5:27/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:5:27/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that God accepts from a pure-hearted person and rejected Qābil because he was not pure-hearted.
TABRISI:5:27/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أراد إنما يتقبل الله ممن كان زاكي القلب

TABRISI:5:27/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:27/r12.claim: He rejects the inference that no obedience by a sinner can be accepted: reward is due when obedience is done as obedience, and a sinner may act in that deserving way.
TABRISI:5:27/r12.anchor: وهذا لا يصح لأن المعنى أن الثواب إنما يستحقه من يوقع الطاعة

TABRISI:5:27/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:27/r13.claim: The account parallels the Jews' covenant-breaking and indecencies with Adam's son's murder and punishment, consoling the Prophet amid their hostility and rebuking them.
TABRISI:5:27/r13.anchor: أن حال اليهود في نقض العهد وارتكاب الفواحش كارتكاب ابن آدم في قتله أخاه

TABRISI:5:27/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27/r14.speaker: قالوا
TABRISI:5:27/r14.claim: They say Eve bore twins, a boy and girl each time: Qābil and Aqleemā first, then Hābil and Labūdhā; Adam ordered cross-marriage, which Hābil accepted but Qābil refused because his sister was more beautiful.
TABRISI:5:27/r14.anchor: قالوا إن حواء امرأة آدم كانت تلد في كل بطن غلاما وجارية

TABRISI:5:27#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر وغيره من المفسرين
TABRISI:5:27#2/r1.claim: In the story related from Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir and other commentators, Qābil objected to Adam's marriage decision, but agreed to an offering test; Hābil brought the best of his flock, Qābil the worst of his crop, and fire consumed Hābil's gift while sparing Qābil's. Adam was away at Mecca, and Qābil killed Hābil with a stone after threatening him.
TABRISI:5:27#2/r1.anchor: روي ذلك عن أبي جعفر الباقر ع وغيره من المفسرين

TABRISI:5:27#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:27#2/r2.claim: Qābil's heart was impure and he offered inferior property, while Hābil gave his best and inwardly accepted God's decree; this explains why one offering was accepted.
TABRISI:5:27#2/r2.anchor: أن قابيل لم يكن زاكي القلب وقرب بشر ماله وأخسه

TABRISI:5:27#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27#2/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:5:27#2/r3.claim: Another explanation says no poor person was available to receive the offering, so a heavenly fire descended and consumed it.
TABRISI:5:27#2/r3.anchor: سبب أكل النار للقربان أنه لم يكن هناك فقير

TABRISI:5:27#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:27#2/r4.speaker: إسماعيل بن رافع
TABRISI:5:27#2/r4.claim: Ismāʿīl ibn Rāfiʿ reports that Hābil's offering grazed in Paradise until it was made the ransom for Abraham's son.
TABRISI:5:27#2/r4.anchor: إسماعيل بن رافع: أن قربان هابيل كان يرتع في الجنة

THALABI:v4p48/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p48/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p48/r1.claim: The two sons of Adam are Abel (Habil) and Cain (Qabil); Thaʿlabī records three forms for Habil's name and five for Qabil's.
THALABI:v4p48/r1.anchor: واتل عليهم نبأ خبر ابني آدم وهما هابيل وقابيل، فهابيل في اسمه ثلاث لغات

THALABI:v4p48/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p48/r2.speaker: أهل العلم بالقرآن
THALABI:v4p48/r2.claim: Scholars say Eve bore Adam twins, a boy and girl, in each pregnancy except Seth, who was born alone; she had forty children across twenty pregnancies, from Cain and Aqlima to ʿAbd al-Mughith and his twin.
THALABI:v4p48/r2.anchor: وكان سبب تقربهما القربان على ما ذكره أهل العلم بالقرآن. أن حواء كانت تلد لآدم (عليه السلام) توأما

THALABI:v4p48/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p48/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p48/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Adam lived until his children and grandchildren numbered forty thousand, and saw among them adultery, wine drinking, and corruption.
THALABI:v4p48/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم يمت آدم (عليه السلام) حتى بلغ ولده وولد ولده أربعين ألفا

THALABI:v4p48/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p48/r4.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v4p48/r4.claim: One account says Adam first approached Eve a hundred years after their descent, and she bore Cain and his twin before Abel and his twin in the next pregnancy.
THALABI:v4p48/r4.anchor: فقال بعضهم: غشى آدم حواء بعد هبوطهما إلى الأرض بمائة سنة فولدت له قابيل وتوأمته أقليما

THALABI:v4p48/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p48/r5.speaker: بعض أهل الكتاب
THALABI:v4p48/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits from People of the Book that Cain and his twin were conceived in Paradise before the sin and born without labor or blood; after descent, Eve's pregnancy with Abel and his twin brought ordinary discomfort and blood.
THALABI:v4p48/r5.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: عن بعض أهل الكتاب، العلم الأول إن آدم كان يغشى حواء في الجنة

THALABI:v4p49/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p49/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p49/r1.claim: In the first generation, when children matured, they married siblings from other pregnancies; a twin sister was forbidden because Eve and her daughters were the only women.
THALABI:v4p49/r1.anchor: وكان آدم إذا شب أولاده تزوج غلام هذا البطن جارية البطن الآخر

THALABI:v4p49/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p49/r2.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v4p49/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says Cain and Aqlima were born first, then Abel and Luwaiza two years later; Adam told Cain to marry Luwaiza and Abel to marry Aqlima, Cain's twin.
THALABI:v4p49/r2.anchor: في قول الكلبي. وأدركوا أمر الله عز وجل آدم (عليه السلام) أن ينكح قابيل ليوذا أخت هابيل

THALABI:v4p49/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p49/r3.speaker: قابيل
THALABI:v4p49/r3.claim: Cain refused the match, claiming his twin was more beautiful, born in Paradise, and rightfully his; Adam answered that she was forbidden and proposed that the accepted offering decide.
THALABI:v4p49/r3.anchor: وقال: هي أختي ولدت معي في بطن. وهي أحسن من أخت هابيل وأنا أحق بها منه

THALABI:v4p49/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p49/r4.speaker: معاوية بن عمار
THALABI:v4p49/r4.claim: Asked al-Sadiq whether Adam married his daughter to his son, Muʿawiya ibn ʿAmmar reports the answer: God forbid; Adam's religion was the same as the Prophet's, who would not accept that.
THALABI:v4p49/r4.anchor: وقال معاوية بن عمار: سألت الصادق عليه سلام الله عن آدم (عليه السلام) أكان زوج ابنته من ابنه، فقال: معاذ الله

THALABI:v4p49/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p49/r5.speaker: الصادق
THALABI:v4p49/r5.claim: Al-Sadiq's alternative account says Eve first bore Luwaiza, then Cain and Abel; God paired Cain with the jinni woman Jihana and Abel with the houri Nuzla, after which Cain envied his brother.
THALABI:v4p49/r5.anchor: فلما أدرك قابيل أظهر الله جنية من ولد الجان يقال لها جهانة في صورة إنسية

THALABI:v4p49/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p49/r6.speaker: آدم
THALABI:v4p49/r6.claim: In al-Sadiq's report, Adam tells Cain that merit belongs to God, who gives it to whom He wills, and proposes the offerings to settle who deserves precedence.
THALABI:v4p49/r6.anchor: فقال له آدم: يا بني إن الفضل بيد الله يؤتيه من يشاء. فقال: لا ولكنك آثرته علي

THALABI:v4p49#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p49#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p49#2/r1.claim: They say an accepted offering was consumed by fire from heaven; if rejected, no fire came and birds or beasts ate it.
THALABI:v4p49#2/r1.anchor: قالوا: وكانت القرابين إذا كانت مقبولة نزلت نار من السماء فأكلتها.

THALABI:v4p49#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p49#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p49#2/r2.claim: Cain, a farmer, offered inferior grain indifferently and intended to marry his twin regardless; Abel, a shepherd, offered his finest lamb, milk, and butter sincerely.
THALABI:v4p49#2/r2.anchor: وكان قابيل صاحب زرع وقرب حبرة من طعام من أردى زرع وأضمر في نفسه: ما أبالي أيقبل مني أم لا

THALABI:v4p49#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p49#2/r3.speaker: إسماعيل بن رافع
THALABI:v4p49#2/r3.claim: Ibn Rafiʿ says Abel prized one lamb above all his wealth and offered it; fire consumed Abel's lamb, milk, and butter, but not Cain's grain, because Abel's heart was pure.
THALABI:v4p49#2/r3.anchor: وقال إسماعيل بن رافع: بلغني أن هابيل أمنح له غنمه وكان في حملتها حمل فأحبه

THALABI:v4p49#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p49#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p49#2/r4.claim: The fire accepted Abel's offering and rejected Cain's; the rejection exposed Cain's envy and malice.
THALABI:v4p49#2/r4.anchor: وقبل قربان هابيل لأنه كان زاكي القلب.

THALABI:v4p49#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p49#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p49#2/r5.claim: The accepted lamb continued grazing in Paradise until it became the ransom for Abraham's son.
THALABI:v4p49#2/r5.anchor: فما زال يرتع في الجنة حتى فدى به ابن إبراهيم فذلك قوله عز وجل فتقبل من أحدهما

THALABI:v4p49#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p49#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p49#2/r6.claim: Before leaving for Mecca to visit the House, Adam asked heaven, earth, and mountains to safeguard his children; all refused, but Cain accepted, then betrayed the trust and killed Abel.
THALABI:v4p49#2/r6.anchor: فلما أراد أن يأتي مكة قال للسماء: احفظي ولدي بالأمانة فأبت، وقال ذلك للأرض فأبت

THALABI:v4p49#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p49#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p49#2/r7.claim: Thaʿlabī links Cain's bearing and betraying the trust to 33:72, which says the heavens, earth, and mountains declined it while the human being bore it, unjust and ignorant.
THALABI:v4p49#2/r7.anchor: وفي ذلك قوله إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السماوات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها

THALABI:v4p49#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p49#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p49#2/r8.claim: While Adam was away, Cain threatened Abel in Gaza, resenting the accepted offering, the marriage pairing, and the public view that Abel was better; Abel replied that God accepts only from the God-fearing.
THALABI:v4p49#2/r8.anchor: قالوا: فلما غاب آدم أتى قابيل وهابيل وهو في غزة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the brothers as Habil and Qabil: Habil offered his best ram, while Qabil offered poor grain; heavenly fire accepted Habil's offering, not Qabil's, provoking jealousy and the threat to kill. The ram was also said to be the one by which God ransomed Ishmael.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: {واتل عليهم} يا محمد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r2.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r2.claim: Unlike the other exegetes, al-Hasan and al-Dahhak say the offerers were two Israelites, not Adam's biological sons.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r2.anchor: إلا الحسن والضحاك فإنهما قالا: إن ابني آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r3.claim: The commentary has discussed the meaning of qurban in Surat Al Imran.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r3.anchor: ومضى الكلام في معنى القربان في سورة آل عمران

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r4.claim: The dual verb implies that each brother brought an offering, although the noun is singular.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r4.anchor: قرب كل واحد منهما قربانا، نجمعهما في الفعل وأفرد الاسم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r5.claim: Qurban may be a collective noun that serves for one or many, or a verbal noun like rajahan, ʿudwan, and kufran, formed from a verb meaning to draw near to God by offering property.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: إن القربان اسم جنس، فهو يصلح للواحد وللعدد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r6.claim: In earlier practice, a person seeking something from God preceded the request with a sacrificial offering; it was called qurban because it brought the offerer near to God, and verbal nouns do not take dual or plural forms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p334#2/r6.anchor: وكان الرجل فيما مضى إذا رفع إلى الله حاجة قدم أمامها نسيكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r1.claim: Al-Farra says the speaker is elided: the brother whose offering was rejected threatened the other, as context makes clear; Arabic can similarly omit an intended subject in familiar paired situations.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r1.anchor: قاله الفراء (¬1). ومثله في الكلام أن تقول إذا اجتمع السفيه والحليم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r2.claim: Qarraba here means to offer a sacrifice and draw near to God with one's property, not to approach a place or make something physically nearer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r2.anchor: ليس معناه من القريب الذي هو ضد البعيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r3.claim: The pious are those who refrain from sins; the wording leaves the feared object implicit because sin is what most deserves to be feared.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r3.anchor: فأطلق للعلم بأن المراد أنها أحق ما يجب أن يخاف منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Habil explained that God accepts only from someone pure in heart, and rejected Qabil because his heart was not pure.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p336/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قال له هابيل: إنما يتقبل الله ممن كان زاكي القلب

QASHANI:5:27/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:27/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:27/r1.claim: The two sons of Adam symbolize the heart's Abel, the intellect, and Cain, the estimative faculty; each has a twin faculty.
QASHANI:5:27/r1.anchor: القلب للذين هما هابيل القلب وقابيل الوهم، إذ كان لكل منهما توأمة.

QASHANI:5:27/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:27/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:27/r2.claim: The intellect's twin is the practical, deliberative rational faculty, which orders worldly and spiritual life and derives virtuous actions, character, crafts, and governance.
QASHANI:5:27/r2.anchor: أما توأمة العقل فالعاقلة العلمية المدبرة لأمور المعاش والمعاد بالآراء الصلاحية المقتضية للأعمال الصالحة

QASHANI:5:27/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:27/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:27/r3.claim: The estimative faculty's twin is imagination, which handles sensory and particular meanings in service of satanic opinions.
QASHANI:5:27/r3.anchor: وأما توأمة الوهم: فالقوة المتخيلة المتصرفة في المحسوسات والمعاني الجزئية لتحصيل الآراء الشيطانية

QASHANI:5:27/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:27/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:27/r4.claim: The heart pairs estimation with practical reason so demonstrative reasoning and spiritual discipline subdue it to intellect, service, truthful hope, and good works.
QASHANI:5:27/r4.anchor: فأمر آدم القلب بتزويج الوهم بتوأمة العقل التي هي العاقلة العلمية لتتسلط عليه بالقياسات العقلية البرهانية

QASHANI:5:27/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:27/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:27/r5.claim: The heart also pairs intellect with imagination, making imagination useful for universal and particular knowledge while curbing corrupt fantasies and false inner talk.
QASHANI:5:27/r5.anchor: وتزويج العقل توأمة الوهم ليجعلها صالحة ويمنعها عن شهوات التخيلات الفاسدة

QASHANI:5:27/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:27/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:27/r6.claim: Cain-estimation envies Abel-intellect because the intellect's twin is more beautiful and beloved through her affinity with him.
QASHANI:5:27/r6.anchor: فحسد قابيل الوهم هابيل العقل لكون توأمته أجمل عنده وأحب لمناسبتها إياه

QASHANI:5:27/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:27/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:27/r7.claim: The heart asks each faculty for an offering: intellect offers a valid universal intelligible by yielding a sound conclusion and dissolving the syllogism's form.
QASHANI:5:27/r7.anchor: أن يقرب كل واحد منهما قربانا أي: نسكا يتقرب به إلى الله بإفاضة النتيجة وإفناء صورة القياس

QASHANI:5:27/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:27/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:27/r8.claim: Intellect's offering is accepted because its universal intelligible conforms to reality; estimation's fallacious or partial imagined form is rejected as nonconforming.
QASHANI:5:27/r8.anchor: وقبول الصورة المعقولة الكلية المطابقة لما في نفس الأمر التي هي نسيكته التي يتقرب بها إلى الله

QASHANI:5:27/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:27/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:27/r9.claim: Estimation's offering is not accepted because it yields no conclusion and its imaginary image does not match reality, deepening its envy.
QASHANI:5:27/r9.anchor: وعدم قبول قربان الوهم الذي هو صورة المغالطة أو الصورة الموهومة الجزئية امتناع اتصال العقل به

QASHANI:5:27#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:27#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:27#2/r1.claim: As intellect draws nearer to God and leaves estimation behind, estimation tries to undo its work through doubts opposing reason in difficult theoretical inquiry.
QASHANI:5:27#2/r1.anchor: لما زاد قرب العقل من الله وبعده عن رتبة الوهم في مدركاته وتصرفاته كان الوهم أحرص على إبطال عمله

QASHANI:5:27#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:27#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:27#2/r2.claim: Killing means stopping intellect's proper activity and cutting off the spirit's aid and the guidance-light that sustains it.
QASHANI:5:27#2/r2.anchor: وقتله عبارة عن منعه عن فعله وقطع مدد الروح ونور الهداية الذي به حياة العقل عنه

QASHANI:5:27#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:27#2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:27#2/r3.claim: The God-fearing either take God as protection when doing good or guard against dark bodily dispositions, lies, misguidance, destructive desires, and ruinous suggestions.
QASHANI:5:27#2/r3.anchor: الذين يتخذون الله وقاية في صدور الخيرات منهم أو يحذرون آثام الهيئات المظلمة البدنية والأكاذيب الباطلة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r1.claim: The two sons are Abel and Cain.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r1.anchor: { واتل عليهم } يعني: على قومك { نبأ } خبر { ابني آدم } هابيل وقابيل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r2.claim: Abel offered his best ram, which heavenly fire carried away; al-Wahidi identifies it as the ram that ransomed Ishmael. Cain offered inferior wheat, which the fire did not take.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r2.anchor: { إذ قربا قربانا } تقرب إلى الله هابيل بخير كبش في غنمه، فنزلت من السماء نار فاحتملته، فهو الكبش الذي فدي به إسماعيل،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r3.claim: Qurban is any offering made to draw near to God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r3.anchor: وكان صاحب زرع، فلم تحمل النار قربانه، والقربان: اسم لكل ما يتقرب به إلى الله،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r4.claim: The rejected brother threatened Abel out of envy; Abel says God accepts from those who avoid sins, not disobedient people.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r4.anchor: فقال الذي لم يتقبل منه: { لأقتلنك } حسدا له، فقال هابيل: { إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين } للمعاصي [لا من العاصين].

ELMALILI:5:27-31/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r1.speaker: Ekser müfessirîn
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r1.claim: Most commentators identify Adam’s two sons as his biological sons Qābil and Hābil.
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r1.anchor: Ekser müfessirîn bu iki Âdem oğlu Hazret-i Âdem’in sulbî oğulları olan Kābil ve Hâbil olduğunu söylemişler

ELMALILI:5:27-31/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r2.speaker: Hasan ve Dahhâk
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r2.claim: Hasan and Dahhāk identify them as two Israelites, using the story’s later phrase “because of that” as evidence.

ELMALILI:5:27-31/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r3.claim: Exact identities are unnecessary to benefit from the account: the general wording emphasizes the event rather than legends, and even a hypothetical story would have a true application in Israelite history.
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r3.anchor: kıssadan istifade için eşhâsın ta‘yîn-i hüviyetleri lâzım olmadığından ale’l-ıtlâk

ELMALILI:5:27-31/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r4.claim: Because many marvel-filled tales circulate under Qābil and Hābil’s names, “in truth” directs attention to the event’s reality rather than fables.
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r4.anchor: بِٱلْحَقِّ kaydıyla da efsanelere değil, zât-ı vak‘anın hakikatine celb-i dikkat edilmiştir

ELMALILI:5:27-31/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r5.claim: A hadith says God gave people the two sons of Adam as a parable and told them to take its good and leave its evil.
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r5.anchor: Bir hadîs-i şerifte vârid olmuştur ki: “Allah teâlâ size iki Âdemoğlu ile bir mesel darb etti, bunun hayrını tutun, şerrini bırakın.”

ELMALILI:5:27-31/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r6.claim: Qurbān is not limited to a slaughtered animal; it means anything offered to draw near to God, including sacrifices and other alms.
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r6.anchor: asıl mânası Allah’a tekarrub için arz u takdim edilen herhangi bir şey demektir ki gerek zebîha ve gerek diğer sadakalardan e‘amdır

ELMALILI:5:27-31/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r7.claim: One offering was accepted and the other was not; the rejected brother envied the accepted one and threatened to kill him.
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r7.anchor: kurbanı kabul edilmeyen öbürüne hased ederek

ELMALILI:5:27-31/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r8.claim: The brother answers that God accepts only from the God-fearing, urging his attacker to fear God and correct his intention.
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r8.anchor: Allah ancak müttakīlerden kabul eder. Binâen‘aleyh Allah’tan kork, niyetini tashih et

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r1.claim: Qurban lexically means approaching or something that brings one near to God; technically it is an animal slaughtered properly under specified conditions and at a specified time for worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r1.anchor: Sözlükte “yaklaşmak, yakın olmak, Allah’a yakınlık sağlamaya vesile kılınan şey” anlamlarına gelen kurban kelimesi, dinî bir terim olarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r2.claim: The Qur’an uses qurban three times: for a heavenly-fire sacrifice requested by Israelites, Adam’s sons’ offerings, and idols treated by polytheists as means of nearness to God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r2.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de üç yerde geçmektedir. Bunlardan birinde İsrâiloğulları’nın herhangi bir peygamberden mûcize olarak istedikleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r3.claim: Across history religions have offered varied sacrifices, including plants, grain, money, animals, and even human beings; the offerings, methods, and purposes differ.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r3.anchor: Tarih boyunca bütün dinlerde Tanrı’ya kurban sunma uygulamalarının bulunduğu tesbit edilebilmekte; fakat kurbanlıklar, kurban sunma şekilleri ve amaçları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r4.claim: The relevant Hajj passage indicates that all revealed religions have an animal-slaughter sacrifice performed as worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r4.anchor: Hac sûresinin ilgili âyetinden (22/34-37) ilâhî dinlerin hepsinde “ibadet amacıyla hayvan kesme” anlamında kurban ibadetinin bulunduğu anlaşılmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r5.claim: Christianity gives Jesus’ crucifixion a special sacrificial meaning, believing God gave him for humanity’s sin; the Qur’an rejects human sacrifice and recounts Abraham and Ishmael’s successful submission followed by an animal sent as a divine gift.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r5.anchor: Bu inancın, insan için insanın kurban edilmesi anlamını içermesine karşılık Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de Hz. İbrâhim ve oğlu Hz. İsmâil’in Allah’ın buyruğuna

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r6.claim: Sacrificing at Eid al-Adha became a religious ruling in Islam in 2 AH, established by the Qur’an, Sunnah, and consensus.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r6.anchor: İslâm’da, kurban bayramında kurban kesmenin dinî bir hüküm oluşu kitap, sünnet ve icmâ ile sabit olup, hicretin 2. yılında konulmuştur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r7.speaker: Ebû Hanîfe
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r7.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that anyone meeting the religious conditions must sacrifice during Eid al-Adha; most scholars instead call it a confirmed Sunnah.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r7.anchor: Dinen aranan şartları taşıyan kimselerin kurban bayramında kurban kesmeleri Ebû Hanîfe’ye göre vâciptir. Çoğunluğa göre ise müekked sünnettir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r8.speaker: Ebû Hanîfe ve aynı görüşü paylaşanlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r8.claim: Abu Hanifa’s school adduces hadiths and the command to sacrifice in 108:2; it regards the verse’s transmission as certain but its legal indication as probabilistic, enough to establish obligation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r8.anchor: Ebû Hanîfe ve aynı görüşü paylaşanlar, konuyla ilgili hadislerin yanı sıra Kevser sûresinin 2. âyetinde geçen “... Kurban kes” emrini de delil olarak getirmişler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r9.claim: The statement in 37:107 that a great sacrificial animal was given in exchange for Abraham’s son is also cited as evidence that sacrifice is legitimate.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r9.anchor: Sâffât sûresinin “Biz, (oğlunun canına) bedel olarak ona iri bir kurbanlık verdik” meâlindeki 107. âyeti de kurban ibadetinin meşrûiyetine delil olarak gösterilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r10.speaker: Çoğunluğa
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r10.claim: The majority considers Eid sacrifice a confirmed Sunnah, not an obligation.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r11.speaker: Kurban kesmenin sünnet olduğu kanaatini taşıyan bilginler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r11.claim: They read the hadith’s if-you-wish clause as leaving sacrifice to personal choice; the Prophet’s consistent practice and reports of its merit establish Sunnah status rather than obligation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r11.anchor: Bu bilginlere göre hadisteki “biriniz kurban kesmek isterse” ifadesinde yer alan “isterse” kaydı kurbanın vâcip olmayıp şahsın iradesine bırakılmış olduğunu gösterir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r12.claim: Besides Eid sacrifices, sacrifices become obligatory when vowed, and may also be offered voluntarily for God’s pleasure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r12.anchor: Kurban bayramında kesilen kurban dışında, adandığı için vâcip olan veya Allah rızâsı için (nâfile olarak) kesilen kurbanlar da vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r13.claim: After recounting Moses and his people as a lesson especially for the Jews of Medina, God instructs the Prophet to relate Adam’s two sons as another admonition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r13.anchor: Yüce Allah önceki âyetlerde özellikle Medine yahudileri için ibret olsun diye Hz. Mûsâ ile kavmi arasında geçen bazı olayları anlattıktan sonra

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r14.claim: The account was revealed to expose how far envy can lead: one of Adam’s sons became the first to shed blood, killing his brother and opening an evil precedent for humanity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r14.anchor: Çünkü Âdem’in oğullarından biri kıskançlığı sebebiyle yeryüzünde ilk defa kan dökerek kardeşini öldürmüş, insanlık için kötü bir çığır açmıştı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r15.claim: The next verse’s rule that killing one person unjustly is like killing all humanity, and saving one is like saving all, is a universal human-rights principle first stated as a law for the Israelites.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r15.anchor: Bir cana kıymaya veya yeryüzünde fesat çıkarmaya karşılık olmaksızın kim bir kimseyi öldürürse bütün insanları öldürmüş gibi olur. Kim de bir canı kurtarırsa

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r16.speaker: İbn Kesîr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r16.claim: A narration says Habil and Qabil disputed; Adam told them both to offer a sacrifice, with acceptance deciding who was right, and heavenly fire consuming an accepted offering; Habil’s was accepted and the jealous Qabil killed him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r16.anchor: Sunulan kurbanlardan Hâbil’inki kabul edildi. Kıskançlığı yüzünden bu durumu içine sindiremeyen Kabil, kardeşini öldürdü (İbn Kesîr, III, 76).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r17.claim: The Torah also tells this story and calls Qabil Cain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r17.anchor: Olay Tevrat’ta da anlatılmakta, ancak Kabil’in ismi Kain olarak geçmektedir (Tekvîn, 4/1-16).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r18.speaker: efsanvî olduğunu söyleyenler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r18.claim: Some have regarded the story and its characters as mythical.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r18.anchor: Olayın ve kişilerin efsanevî olduğunu söyleyenler olmuşsa da bu görüş Kur’an ve Tevrat’ta anlatılanlara aykırıdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r19.speaker: Ömer Faruk Harman
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r19.claim: Parallels in ancient mythologies do not make the Qur’anic and biblical account mythical: cultural variants naturally change while deriving from a historical event; the Torah’s fuller account likely incorporates multiple traditions, while revealed religions trace humanity to Adam and Eve.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r19.anchor: farklı unsurları hikâyeye katmıştır” (Ömer Faruk Harman, “Hâbil ve Kabil”, DİA, XIV, 376-378).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r20.speaker: Hasan-ı Basrî ve bir kısım müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r20.claim: They say the two men were Israelites rather than Adam’s own sons, called Adam’s sons because all people descend from him; their story portrays Israelite excesses, especially envy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r20.anchor: Tâbiînden Hasan-ı Basrî ve bir kısım müfessirlere göre burada anlatılanlar Hz. Âdem’in kendi oğulları değil, İsrâiloğulları’ndan iki şahıstır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r21.claim: The author rejects the Israelite-identification view: the following account says one brother learned burial from a crow, whereas Israelites could not have been ignorant of how to bury the dead.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:27/r21.anchor: Ancak bu yorum âyetteki diğer bilgilerle uyumlu görünmemektedir. Zira daha sonraki âyetlerde bildirildiğine göre bu iki kardeşten biri diğerini öldürmüş, fakat naaşını nasıl gömeceğini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r8.claim: The story implies that Adam’s children believed in God, the afterlife, reckoning, punishment, and Hell, and understood piety, fear of God, and worship through sacrifice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r8.anchor: Kıssadan Hz. Âdem’in çocuklarının Allah’a, âhirete, hesaba, cezaya ve cehenneme inandıkları; Allah korkusu ve takvâ gibi konularda bilinç sahip oldukları

BURHAN:v1p155/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p155/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p155/r11.claim: The two sons of Adam in the narrative are Cain and Abel.

BURHAN:v2p144/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p144/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p144/r2.claim: The Prophet says an initiator of a good practice earns its reward and an initiator of a bad one bears its sin and the followers' burden; the source also links this to Adam's sons.
BURHAN:v2p144/r2.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من سن فى الإسلام سنة حسنة فله أجرها وأجر من عمل بها

SULAMI:v1p176#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p176#4/r1.speaker: ممشاد الدينوري
SULAMI:v1p176#4/r1.claim: Memshad al-Dinawari assigns Adam's sin to greed, Iblis's to pride, and Cain's to envy: greed deprives, pride humiliates, and envy abandons its victim.
SULAMI:v1p176#4/r1.anchor: قال ممشاد الدينوري : كان معصية آدم من الحرص

SULAMI:v1p176#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p176#4/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p176#4/r2.claim: Sahl says piety and sincerity are the heart's receptacles for the limbs' deeds.
SULAMI:v1p176#4/r2.anchor: قال سهل : التقوى والإخلاص محلا القلوب لأعمال الجوارح

SULAMI:v1p176#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p176#4/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p176#4/r3.claim: Ibn Ata identifies the pious as those sincere to God in what they say and do.
SULAMI:v1p176#4/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : المخلصين له فيما يقولون ويعملون

SULAMI:v1p176#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p176#4/r4.speaker: السلامي
SULAMI:v1p176#4/r4.claim: Al-Sulami says offerings differ, but the nearest is the act God has promised to accept; that promise is truthful, and prostration is the place of nearness through remembrance.
SULAMI:v1p176#4/r4.anchor: قال السلامي : القرابين مختلفة وأقرب القرابين ما وعد الله جل وعز بقبوله

ITQAN:v4p385/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p385/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p385/r1.claim: The two sons of Adam in the account are Cain and Abel, and Abel is the one killed.

ITQAN:v2p479/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p479/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p479/r5.claim: عن can mean من; the parallel wording فتقبل من أحدهما supports reading عن عباده as من عباده.
ITQAN:v2p479/r5.anchor: أي منهم بدليل ﴿ فتقبل من أحدهما ﴾

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p345/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p345/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p345/r1.claim: Eloquence does not reside in sound or a bare idea alone: skilled composition gives common meanings new images and qualities, like a craftsperson transforming plain jewelry.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p345/r1.anchor: الشاعر قد عمد إلى معنى مبتذل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p345/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p345/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p345/r2.claim: The claim that only word and meaning exist forces any excellence between expressions with the same aim to belong to sound alone, a false reduction that ignores the image formed in meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p345/r2.anchor: فقالوا : إنه ليس إلا المعنى واللفظ ولا ثالث

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p345/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p345/r3.speaker: الجاحظ
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p345/r3.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ says meanings are common property and poetry is craftsmanship and image-making; Jurjānī says critics use “word” to mean this crafted image, not phonetic sound.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p345/r3.anchor: الذي عناه الجاحظ حيث قال : وذهب الشيخ

DAMGHANI:v1p374/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r11.claim: Qurbān means an offering that draws one near to God.
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r11.anchor: القربان القرب إلى الله تعالى قوله سبحانه في سورة المائدة إذ قربا قربانا

AKHFASH:v1p279/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p279/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p279/r1.claim: The hamza of nabaʾ is retained because it derives from anbaʾtuhu; the alif of ibn drops as a hamzat waṣl, and in pause nabaʾ is shortened rather than made nabā because it is annexed.
AKHFASH:v1p279/r1.anchor: فالهمزة ل"نبأ" لأنها من "أنباته". وألف "ابني" تذهب

AKHFASH:v1p279/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p279/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p279/r2.claim: When stopping on nabaʾ, he says to shorten the form, not say nabā, since it is in an annexation construction.
AKHFASH:v1p279/r2.anchor: واذا وقفت [قلت] "نبأ" مقصور ولا تقول "نبا" لأنها مضاف

FARRA:v1p304/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p304/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p304/r5.claim: The unexpressed speaker of ‘I will surely kill you’ is the brother whose offering was not accepted, as the jealousy context makes clear despite two possible antecedents.
FARRA:v1p304/r5.anchor: الذي لم يتقبل منه هو القائل لحسده

FARRA:v1p304/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p304/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p304/r6.claim: Arabic lets context resolve an omitted subject when paired candidates contrast clearly, as in praising the wise or helping the oppressed; it fails when neither candidate is distinguished.
FARRA:v1p304/r6.anchor: ومثله في الكلام أن تقول: إذا اجتمع السفيه والحليم حمد، تنوي بالحمد الحليم، وإذا رأيت الظالم والمظلوم أعنت

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#4/r1.claim: Nabaʾ means a report or account.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#4/r1.anchor: {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم} أي خبرهما.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#4/r2.claim: A qurbān is anything offered to draw near to God, including a slaughtered offering or another gift.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#4/r2.anchor: و (القربان) : ما تقرب به إلى الله من ذبح وغيره.

NAHHAS:v2p14/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p14/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p14/r10.claim: The verb is imperative; its wāw is dropped.
NAHHAS:v2p14/r10.anchor: أمر فلذلك حذفت منه الواو أمر الله تعالى النبي

NAHHAS:v2p14/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p14/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p14/r11.claim: God commands the Prophet to recount the story to the Jews to answer their rejection of him; it shows they are no more honored than Adam’s sons and supports Muhammad’s prophethood because he had not read books.
NAHHAS:v2p14/r11.anchor: أمر الله تعالى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يتلو على اليهود خبر ابني آدم

NAHHAS:v2p14/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p14/r12.speaker: عمرو ومجاهد
NAHHAS:v2p14/r12.claim: Amr and Mujahid say the offerers were Israelites; Abu Jaʿfar rejects this because the next verse says the killer was shown how to bury his brother.
NAHHAS:v2p14/r12.anchor: وأما قول عمرو مجاهد إن اللذين قربا قربانا من بني إسرائيل فغلط

NAHHAS:v2p14/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p14/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p14/r13.claim: The pious from whom God accepts offerings are those who avoid sins.

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r1.claim: One analysis makes bi-l-haqq circumstantial to the reciter: recite while adhering to truth and sincerity.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r1.anchor: اتل ذلك حال كونك ملتبسا بالحق

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r2.claim: A second analysis makes it circumstantial to nabāʾ: the account is truthful and agrees with earlier scriptures, establishing proof of the Messenger’s mission.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r2.anchor: اتل نبأهما ملتبسا بالصدق موافقا لما في كتب الأولين

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r3.claim: A third analysis makes it an adjective of an implicit verbal noun: recite a recitation marked by truth and sincerity.
