SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r3.anchor: اتل ذلك تلاوة ملتبسة بالحق والصدق

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r4.claim: Al-Samīn suggests al-Zamakhsharī prefers the verbal-noun analysis, since he lists it first; in all three, bāʾ conveys accompaniment and attaches to an omitted phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r4.anchor: وكأنه اختيار الزمخشري إذ به بدأ

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the mīm in Ādam with sukūn before bāʾ in al-ḥaqq; likewise any mīm preceded by a vowel and followed by bāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بسكون الميم من " آدم "

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r6.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r6.claim: They attach idh to nabāʾ itself: the account is their story at that time; al-Samīn calls this clear.

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats idh as a substitute for nabāʾ, supplying an omitted noun: “the account of that time.”
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r7.anchor: نبأ ذلك الوقت، كذا قدره الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r8.claim: The Shaykh rejects the substitution because idh can be annexed only to a time, whereas nabāʾ is not a time.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r8.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ولا يجوز ما ذكر

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r9.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r9.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ offers a third analysis: idh is circumstantial to nabāʾ and depends on an omitted phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r9.anchor: أنه حال من " نبأ " وعلى هذا

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r10.claim: Al-Samīn finds the third analysis unclear and agrees that idh cannot be a temporal adverb for the future command recite.

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes qur bān as the name of something offered to draw near to God, analogizing it to ḥulwān, what is given.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r11.anchor: به قال الزمخشري - أنه اسم لما يتقرب به

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r12.speaker: الأصمعي
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r12.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī cites “تقربوا قرف القمع” to show that taqarraba can take bāʾ and mean qarraba, supporting the proposed reflexive construction.

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r13.claim: On this derivation, the wording implies “they offered it and so drew near by it”; al-Samīn judges this construction remote.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r13.anchor: إذ قرباه فتقربا به، وفيه بعد

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r14.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r14.claim: The Shaykh objects that تقرب بصدقة is not the passive response to قرب صدقة: both verbs have the same agent, unlike true mutual or passive change.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r14.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وليس " تقرب بصدقة " مطاوع

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r15.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r15.claim: Al-Samīn challenges the Shaykh’s rule, saying he does not accept that account of the construction.

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r16.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r16.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r16.claim: Another analysis treats qur bān as originally a verbal noun later applied to the thing offered, like “Yemeni weaving” and “the prince’s striking.”
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r16.anchor: أن يكون في الأصل مصدرا ثم أطلق على الشيء المتقرب به

SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r17.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r17.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r17.claim: Its singular form supports the verbal-noun analysis: although Cain and Abel each had an offering, the original form would have been dual qur bānayn.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27/r17.anchor: ويؤيد ذلك أنه لم يثن والموضع موضع تثنية

SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r1.claim: The speaker threatening murder is the brother whose offering was not accepted, addressing the brother whose offering was accepted.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r1.anchor: قال الذي لم يتقبل منه للمقبول منه

SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r2.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r2.claim: The majority read the threat with a doubled nūn.

SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r3.claim: The threat is the answer to an omitted oath.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r3.anchor: وهذا جواب قسم محذوف، وقرأه زيد بالخفيفة

SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r4.speaker: زيد
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r4.claim: Zayd reads the threat with a light nūn.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r4.anchor: قرأه زيد بالخفيفة. قال: إنما يتقبل الله

SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r5.claim: The omitted object of “God accepts” is understood as their offerings and deeds.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r5.anchor: مفعوله محذوف لدلالة المعنى عليه أي: قرابينهم وأعمالهم

SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, the verb is used without an intended object, as in “as for one who gives and is mindful.”
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r6.anchor: ويجوز ألا يراد له مفعول كقوله

SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies an omitted exchange: why kill me when I have done no wrong and am not to blame for God accepting my offering instead of yours?
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو محمد بن عطية: " قبلها كلام محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r8.speaker: غيره
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r8.claim: Another commentator also posits a lengthy ellipsis and gives a similar reconstruction.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r8.anchor: وقال غيره: " فيه حذف يطول " وذكر نحوه

SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r9.claim: Al-Samīn sees no need for a long reconstruction: the threat arises from envy at the accepted offering, and the reply hints that piety is the cause of acceptance.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r9.anchor: إذ المعاني المفهومة من فحوى الكلام إذا قدرت قصيرة كان أحسن

SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the reply as telling the envious brother that he brought this on himself by shedding the garment of piety.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r10.anchor: الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: كيف كان قوله: { إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين }

SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r11.claim: Al-Samīn classifies al-Zamakhsharī’s explanation as interpretation of the meaning, not grammatical parsing.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r11.anchor: وهذا ونحوه من تفسير المعنى لا الإعراب

SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r12.claim: One view makes the acceptance statement an interjection between the killer’s threat and the victim’s speech, with “he said” referring to God addressing the Messenger.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: إن هذه الجملة اعتراض بين كلام القاتل وبين كلام المقتول

SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r13.claim: Al-Samīn calls the divine-interjection reading extremely remote because it disrupts the sequence of speech between Cain and Abel.
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r13.anchor: وهو في غاية البعد لتنافر النظم

SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r14.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:5:27#2/r14.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī answers that the singular means each one offered an offering, as in the command to flog each person eighty times.

ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r2.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r2.claim: One report identifies the two as Israelites, since in their era fire consumed an accepted sacrifice; the source cites the demand for a fire-consumed offering.
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r2.anchor: قيل كانا رجلين من بني إسرائيل لأن القربان كان تأكله النار

ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r3.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r3.claim: Another view identifies them as Adam's own sons, Abel and Cain, who each offered a sacrifice.
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r3.anchor: وقيل ابنا آدم لصلبه، أحدهما هابيل والآخر قابيل، فقربا قربانا.

ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r4.claim: A descending fire consuming an offering signaled acceptance: it consumed Abel's offering, not Cain's, prompting Cain's envy and threat.
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r4.anchor: فذلك علامة قبول القربان، فنزلت النار وأكلت قربان هابيل، ولم تأكل قربان قابيل.

ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r5.claim: The omitted subject of قال is the brother whose sacrifice was rejected; context supplies the omission.
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r5.anchor: المعنى قال الذي لم يتقبل منه لاقتلنك، وحذف ذكر الذي لم يتقبل منه

ASAD-NOTES:5:26#n35/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:5:26#n35/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:5:26#n35/r1.claim: The two sons of Adam in the story are Cain and Abel, also known from Genesis 4:1–16.
ASAD-NOTES:5:26#n35/r1.anchor: the story of Cain and Abel, mentioned in Genesis iv, 1-16

ASAD-NOTES:5:26#n35/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:5:26#n35/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:5:26#n35/r2.claim: The pronoun in “tell them” refers to the followers of the Bible and connects the passage with 5:15.
ASAD-NOTES:5:26#n35/r2.anchor: The pronoun in "tell them" refers to the followers of the Bible, and obviously connects with verse 15 of this surah

ASAD-NOTES:5:26#n35/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:5:26#n35/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:5:26#n35/r3.claim: Asad says the Bible followers’ concealed moral in the story is summarized in 5:32.
ASAD-NOTES:5:26#n35/r3.anchor: The moral of this particular Biblical story - a moral which the followers of the Bible have been "concealing from themselves" - is summarized in verse 32.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.claim: The indefinite predicate in ما كان أحد مثلك or خيرا منك is informative under broad negation: it denies anyone equal to or exceeding the person addressed.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.claim: An affirmative كان رجل ذاهبا is uninformative, while adding a specific lineage in كان رجل من آل فلان فارسا can convey new information.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.anchor: أن ذلك في آل فلان وقد يجهله

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.claim: أحد is used for general negation; ما أتاك رجل can deny a particular count, gender, or strength, whereas ما أتاك أحد denies all such possibilities.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.claim: With an established locative predicate, the adjective follows the name in nominative; when the locative is syntactically canceled, the adjective is accusative, and both orders are attested.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.anchor: وتقول ما كان فيها أحد خير منك

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.claim: A required locative is better placed early, while an optional, canceled locative is better delayed; Sībawayh compares this ordering to أظن and أحسب.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.anchor: إذا أردت الإلغاء فكلما أخرت الذي تلغيه كان أحسن

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.claim: The Quranic order ولم يكن له كفوا أحد places the optional locative between the predicate and subject; some Bedouins instead say ولم يكن كفوا أحد.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماكانأحدمثلكوماكانأحدخي.anchor: كأنهم أخروها حيث كانت غير مستقرة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: In إي ها الله ذا, hā substitutes for the oath wāw; the following name is genitive, and the alif of hā may be retained or dropped for ease.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.anchor: وذلك قولك إي ها الله ذا تثبت ألف ها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: The construction takes genitive because hā replaces the omitted oath wāw, whose deletion eases pronunciation.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.anchor: الجر لأن قولهم ها صار عوضا من اللفظ بالواو فحذفت تخفيفا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: Al-Khalīl parses dhā as the sworn matter, with الأمر omitted because the expression is frequent; hā is fronted as in other formulas.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.anchor: ذا فزعم الخليل أنه المحلوف عليه كأنه قال إي والله للأمر هذا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: زهير
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: Zuhayr's line attests the oath formula with hā and dhā.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: The alif in آلله can substitute for oath wāw just as hā does; the substitutes do not occur together or with wāw.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.anchor: ومثل ذلك قولهم آ لله لأفعلن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: أفألله لتفعلن uses the alif in the substituting position, unlike a form retaining the oath wāw.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.anchor: وذلك قولك أفألله لتفعلن ألا ترى

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: نعم الله and إي الله are not substitutes for wāw, since they also occur with it in نعم والله and إي والله.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.anchor: وتقول نعم الله لأفعلن وإي الله لأفعلن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: Al-Khalīl parses the first wāw in the cited oath as an oath particle and the next two as conjunctions joining nouns; all swear to one matter.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.anchor: الخليل في قوله عز وجل @QB@ والليل إذا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: He argues that the later wāws coordinate nouns because the first oath already swears to one matter; separate completed oaths would begin new clauses.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.anchor: فقال إنما أقسم بهذه الأشياء على شيء واحد ولو كان

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: Thumma can coordinate oath nouns like wāw; Sibawayh gives examples with repeated oaths and says thumma here functions as wāw.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: After a completed oath clause, a break makes the later oath independent; without a break its noun is genitive by coordination with the first oath noun.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.anchor: قلت والله لآتينك ثم الله لأضربنك فإن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: When the second oath noun is delayed until after a second verb, the verbs are coordinated first and the delayed oath is separate.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.anchor: ويدلك على أنه إذا قال والله لأضربنك ثم لأقتلنك الله

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: A delayed oath noun remains coordinated and genitive when it is linked to the first oath noun and no clause follows to detach it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.anchor: وإذا قلت والله لآتينك ثم الله فإنما أحد الاسمين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: Do not separate a genitive from its coordinating particle; Sibawayh compares this to separating a preposition from its coordinated noun.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.anchor: كان قبيحا خبيثا لأنه فصل بين المجرور والحرف الذي يشركه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونماقبلالمحلوفبهعوضا.claim: Repeating an oath with another wāw is acceptable through a slip or for emphasis; in this use wāw is a preposition.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p561/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p561/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p561/r2.claim: The Qur’an chooses the highest expression suited to the intended meaning and context; Samarrai identifies this precision as its inimitability against Arab eloquence.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p561/r2.anchor: ولقد تفرّد القرآن الكريم باختيار التعبير الأعلى في المعنى المُراد وفي المكان الذي يقتضيه هذا المعنى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p561/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p561/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p561/r3.claim: The non-Qur’anic example distinguishes a verbal noun that means only the act of giving from ʿaṭāʾ, which can mean either good giving or a good gift/wealth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p561/r3.anchor: أما العطاء فهو اسم المصدر بمعنى الإعطاء أو المال والعطاء يحتمل معنيين إعطاء حسن ومال حسن

NASHR:v1p233/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p233/r10.speaker: السجاوندي
NASHR:v1p233/r10.claim: Sajawandi requires stopping after “واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق” and beginning “إذ قربا قربانا” so the verb “واتل” is not taken as governing “إذ.”
NASHR:v1p233/r10.anchor: ونحو واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق والابتداء إذ قربا قربانا ونحو واتل عليهم نبأ نوح

NASHR:v2p26#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p26#3/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p26#3/r1.claim: Ikhfa applies before the fifteen letters tāʾ, thāʾ, jīm, dāl, dhāl, zāy, sīn, shīn, ṣād, ḍād, ṭāʾ, ẓāʾ, fāʾ, qāf, and kāf; the source gives Quranic examples for each.
NASHR:v2p26#3/r1.anchor: وهو عند باقي حروف المعجم وجملتها خمسة عشر حرفا وهي: التاء، والثاء، والجيم، والدال، والذال

NASHR:v2p26#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p26#3/r2.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v2p26#3/r2.claim: Al-Dani defines ikhfa as intermediate between clear pronunciation and assimilation: the nasal is neither close enough to assimilate nor distant enough to pronounce clearly.
NASHR:v2p26#3/r2.anchor: قال الداني: وذلك أن النون والتنوين لم يقربا من هذه الحروف كقربهما من حروف الإدغام

NASHR:v2p26#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p26#3/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p26#3/r3.claim: The degree of hiding varies with proximity: nearer letters produce stronger ikhfa. A hidden nasal is lightened, while an assimilated nasal is geminated.
NASHR:v2p26#3/r3.anchor: قال: والفرق عند القراء، والنحويين بين المخفي والمدغم أن المخفي مخفف والمدغم مشدد

NASHR:v2p26#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p26#3/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p26#3/r4.claim: For Abu Jaʿfar, noon and tanwin before ghayn and khāʾ also articulate from the nasal cavity, because he treats those letters like oral letters by proximity; other readers retain their original articulation because they classify them as throat letters.
NASHR:v2p26#3/r4.anchor: وحكمهما مع الغين والخاء عند أبي جعفر كذلك، وذلك من حيث أجرى الغين والخاء مجرى حروف الفم

NASHR:v1p419#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p419#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p419#2/r1.claim: Pause-sakt is permitted only on a consonant with no vowel; some silent consonants precede hamza to make it clear, while others receive sakt for a different reason.
NASHR:v1p419#2/r1.anchor: فاعلم أنه لا يجوز السكت إلا على ساكن، إلا أنه لا يجوز السكت على كل ساكن

NASHR:v1p419#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p419#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p419#2/r2.claim: A silent consonant before hamza may be in a separate word or the same word, and may be a long vowel or another consonant; the source lists examples of each combination.
NASHR:v1p419#2/r2.anchor: إما أن يكون منفصلا فيكون آخر كلمة والهمز أول كلمة أخرى، أو يكون متصلا فيكون هو والهمز في كلمة واحدة

NASHR:v1p419#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p419#2/r3.speaker: حمزة، وابن ذكوان، وحفص، ورويس، وإدريس
NASHR:v1p419#2/r3.claim: Sakt in these environments is transmitted through routes of Hamza, Ibn Dhakwan, Hafs, Ruways, and Idris; Hamza’s transmission has the most routes and the greatest disagreement.
NASHR:v1p419#2/r3.anchor: وجاء من هذه الطرق عن حمزة، وابن ذكوان، وحفص، ورويس، وإدريس. فأما حمزة فهو أكثر القراء به عناية

NASHR:v1p419#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p419#2/r4.speaker: جماعة من أهل الأداء
NASHR:v1p419#2/r4.claim: One route through both Khalaf and Khallad pauses on the definite-article lām wherever it occurs and on “شيء” in nominative, genitive, or accusative; this is reported in several manuals.
NASHR:v1p419#2/r4.anchor: ومن روايتي خلف وخلاد في لام التعريف حيث أتت و (شيء) كيف وقعت

NASHR:v1p419#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p419#2/r5.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v1p419#2/r5.claim: In al-Tadhkira, al-Dani’s transmitted versions instead have madd on “شيء” and sakt on the definite-article lām only.
NASHR:v1p419#2/r5.anchor: هو المد في شيء مع السكت على لام التعريف حسب لا غير

NASHR:v2p21/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p21/r5.speaker: صاحب المبهج
NASHR:v2p21/r5.claim: The author rejects al-Mubhij’s anomalous report that Qalun through al-Hulwani and Ibn Buwayyan through Abu Nashit show feminine tāʾ before dāl; showing it before ṭāʾ is also very weak.
NASHR:v2p21/r5.anchor: وشذ صاحب المبهج فحكى عن قالون من طريق الحلواني وابن بويان عن أبي نشيط إظهار تاء التأنيث عند الدال

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies Adam’s two sons as Hābīl and Qābīl; one farmed and the other raised livestock.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم ﴾ قال هما هابيل وقابيل قال كان أحدهما صاحب زرع

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says each brother offered from his property, one bringing the best and one the worst; fire consumed Qābīl’s offering, left the other’s, and Qābīl envied him and threatened to kill him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r2.anchor: فجاء أحدهما بخير ماله وجاء أحدهما بشر ماله فجاءت النار فأكلت قربان أحدهما وهو قابيل وتركت قربان الآخر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports the Prophet saying that Adam’s two sons were made an example for this community and people should follow the better of them; no grading is given.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن ابني آدم ضربا لهذه الأمة مثلا فخذوا بالخير منهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p225/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p225/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p225/r11.claim: The sons-of-Adam story follows Israel’s refusal to fight the giants: Israel shows cowardice, while Cain displays the opposite extreme of audacity in committing murder; both stories concern disobedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p225/r11.anchor: مناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها هو أنه تعالى لما ذكر تمرد بني إسرائيل وعصيانهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r1.claim: The account of Cain and Abel mirrors the preceding passages in attempted violence, disclosure of hidden matters, an ineffective offering, sinful assertion, killing and envy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r1.anchor: وقصة ابني آدم انطوت على مجموع هذه الآيات من بسط اليد، ومن الإخبار بالمغيب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r2.claim: The prior plots include attempted violence, hidden knowledge and ineffective nearness; Israel also rejects Muhammad from envy despite knowing him truthful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r2.anchor: ثم قصة محاربة الجبارين، وتبين أن عدم اتباع بني إسرائيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r3.claim: Wa-utlu ʿalayhim means read and recount to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r3.anchor: ومعنى واتل عليهم: أي اقرأ واسرد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r4.claim: The address most naturally refers to the Israelites, previously discussed and challenged with proofs because they intended to assault the Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r4.anchor: والضمير في عليهم ظاهره أنه يعود على بني إسرائيل إذ هم المحدث عنهم أولا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r5.claim: Believers are informed of obscure matters in earlier scriptures, inaccessible to the Messenger except by revelation; this establishes proof and is a sign of prophethood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r5.anchor: بما هو في غامض كتبهم الأول التي لا تعلق للرسول بها إلا من جهة الوحي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r6.claim: Al-nabaʾ means a report or piece of news.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r6.anchor: والنبأ: هو الخبر. وابنا آدم في قول الجمهور عمر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r7.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r7.claim: The majority, including ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and Qatāda, identify the two as Cain and Abel, Adam’s biological sons.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r7.anchor: وابنا آدم في قول الجمهور عمر، وابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة، وغيرهما: هما قابيل وهابيل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r8.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they were not Adam’s biological sons but two brothers from the Israelites, since sacrifice was prescribed only among the Israelites.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن: لم يكونا ولديه لصلبه، وإنما هما أخوان من بني إسرائيل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says al-Ḥasan is mistaken: it is implausible that Israelites needed a crow to teach burial, and the Prophet calls Cain the first murderer, although killing already occurred among Israelites.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r9.anchor: ووهم الحسن في ذلك. وقيل عليه كيف يجهل الدفن في بني إسرائيل حتى يقتدى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r10.claim: One parsing makes bi-l-ḥaqq a circumstantial phrase attached to the pronoun in wa-utlu, meaning recount accompanied by certain truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r10.anchor: ويحتمل قوله: بالحق، أن يكون حالا من الضمير في: واتل أي: مصحوبا بالحق،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r11.claim: Alternatively, bi-l-ḥaqq describes an omitted verbal noun: a recitation imbued with truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r11.anchor: أو في موضع الصفة لمصدر محذوف أي: تلاوة ملتبسة بالحق،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r12.claim: Idh is governed by nabaʾ and refers to the time of the two men’s story.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r12.anchor: والعامل في إذ نبأ أي حديثهما وقصتهما في ذلك الوقت.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī permits idh as an apposition to al-nabaʾ, meaning the report of that time with an omitted annexed noun; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because idh takes a time noun, whereas nabaʾ is not time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227/r13.anchor:
وقال الزمخشري:
ويجوز أن يكون بدلا من النبأ أي: اتل عليهم النبأ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r1.claim: Commentators recount that Eve bore male-female twins; Adam paired each son with a girl from another birth, but Cain coveted his own beautiful twin Iqlīmiyā over Abel’s less beautiful twin Labūdhā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r1.anchor: وقد طول المفسرون في سبب تقريب هذا القربان وملخصه: أن حواء كانت تلد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r2.claim: One account says Adam ordered the brothers to offer sacrifices after their dispute over the marriage pairing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r2.anchor: ونازع قابيل هابيل في ذلك، فقيل: أمرهما آدم بتقريب القربان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r3.claim: Another account says the brothers offered on their own while Adam, with God’s permission, was away visiting the House in Mecca.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: تقربا من عند أنفسهما، إذ كان آدم غائبا توجه إلى مكة لزيارة البيت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r4.claim: Cain offered crops as a farmer, while Abel, a shepherd, offered a ram.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r4.anchor: والقربان الذي قرباه: هو زرع لقابيل، وكان صاحب زرع، وكبش هابل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r5.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r5.claim: Abel’s offering was accepted and Cain’s rejected; the sign was heavenly fire consuming the accepted offering and leaving the rejected one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r5.anchor: فتقبل من أحدهما وهو هابيل، ولم يتقبل من الآخر وهو قابيل. أي: فتقبل القربان،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid gives the sign in reverse wording: fire consumed the rejected offering and lifted the accepted offering to heaven.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كانت النار تأكل المردود، وترفع المقبول إلى السماء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says taqarraba bi-ṣadaqa is the passive counterpart of qarraba ṣadaqa; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this as a grave error because both verbs retain the same subject, unlike true passive alternation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: يقال: قرب صدقة وتقرب بها، لأن تقرب مطاوع قرب انتهى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r8.claim: Cain’s emphatic threat, with an omitted oath, expresses murderous envy of Abel’s accepted offering and of his claim to the beautiful twin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r8.anchor: هذا وعيد وتهديد شديد، وقد أبرز هذا الخبر مؤكدا بالقسم المحذوف أي: لأقتلنك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r9.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r9.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads la-aqtulannaka with a light nūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: لأقتلنك بالنون الخفيفة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies an omitted question: why kill me when I have done no wrong and am not responsible for God’s accepting my offering?
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن عطية: قبله كلام محذوف تقديره: لم تقتلني وأنا لم أجن شيئا ولا ذنب لي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says Cain’s jealousy came from his own loss of piety, not Abel; he should discipline himself to piety, the cause of acceptance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r11.anchor: لما كان الحسد لأخيه على تقبل قربانه هو الذي حمله على توعده بالقتل قال له: إنما أتيت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the phrase as evidence that God accepts no act of obedience except from a believing, God-fearing person, condemning many who labor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r12.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن الله تعالى لا يقبل طاعة إلا من مؤمن متق، فما أنعاه على أكثر العاملين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r13.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r13.claim: When told at his death that he had lived well, ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh wept because he heard God say that acceptance is only for the God-fearing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p227#2/r13.anchor: وعن عامر بن عبد الله: أنه بكى حين حضرته الوفاة فقيل له: ما يبكيك فقد كنت وكنت:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls al-Zamakhsharī’s explanation an habitual Muʿtazilī insinuation that needs unnecessary assumptions; his own simpler reading is that Cain threatens from envy because piety caused acceptance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r1.anchor: كلامه. ولم يخل من دسيسة الاعتزال على عادته، يحتاج الكلام في فهمه إلى هذه التقديرات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Sunnis agree that fearing God here means avoiding shirk; a monotheist who avoids it has sincerely intended deeds accepted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وأجمع أهل السنة في معنى هذه الألفاظ أنها اتقاه الشرك، فمن اتقاه وهو موحد فأعماله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r3.speaker: عدي بن ثابت
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r3.claim: ʿAdī ibn Thābit and others say the Muslim community’s offering is the prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r3.anchor: وقال عدي بن ثابت وغيره: قربان هذه الأمة الصلاة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r4.claim: The proposal that God speaks this phrase parenthetically to the Messenger, rather than the murdered brother, is not apparent; the pronoun in qāla does not naturally refer to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r4.anchor: وقول من زعم أن قوله: إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين، ليس من كلام المقتول،

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r1.claim: The command to recite is coordinated with an omitted clause connected to the preceding mention of Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r1.anchor: عطف على مقدر تعلق به قوله تعالى : وإذ قال موسى الخ

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r2.claim: One coherence reading makes the story a prelude to Israel's later offenses, after laws were prescribed and messengers brought proofs.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r2.anchor: من حيث أنه تمهيد لما سيأتى إن شاء الله تعالى من جنايات بنى إسرائيل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r3.claim: Another reading contrasts cowardice about killing in the earlier episode with boldness in this killing, while both acts are sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : من حيث أن فى الأول الجبن عن القتل وفى هذا الإقدام عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r4.claim: The pronoun most naturally refers to the Israelites; recitation informs them of obscure material in their scriptures, known to the Prophet only by revelation, establishing proof against them.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r4.anchor: وضمير عليهم يعود على بنى إسرائيل كما هو الظاهر إذ هم المحدث عنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r5.claim: Another view takes the pronoun as referring to Muhammad's community: recite the story to your people.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : الضمير عائد على هذه الأمة أى اتل يا محمد على قومك

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r6.claim: Most exegetes identify the two sons as Habil and Qabil, sons of Adam himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r6.anchor: وكانا باجماع غالب المفسرين ابنى آدم عليه السلام لصلبه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says they were two men from the Children of Israel.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن : كانا رجلين من بنى إسرائيل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿud and other Companions relate that Adam's children were born as boy-girl twins and sibling groups intermarried by necessity; Qabil rejected Habil's request for his more beautiful twin, Aqleema, so Adam made marriage depend on whose offering God accepted.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r8.anchor: ماأخرجه ابن جرير عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r9.claim: In the same report Adam entrusted the sons to the sky, earth, and mountains, all of which declined; Qabil accepted the trust while Adam went to Mecca.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r9.anchor: فقال آدم للسماء : احفظى ولدى بالأمانة فأبت وقال للأرض : فأبت

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r10.claim: Habil offered a ewe, or according to another version a ram; Qabil offered grain, ate its best kernel, and fire consumed Habil's offering as the sign of acceptance while leaving Qabil's untouched.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r10.anchor: فقرب هابيل جذعة وقيل : كبشا وقرب قابيل حزمة سنبل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r11.claim: Adam ordered the test knowing Qabil's offering would not be accepted; he did not mean that acceptance would have made the disputed marriage permissible.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r11.anchor: وإنما أمر بذلك لعلمه أنه لايقبل من قابيل لا أنه لو قبل جاز

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r12.claim: Bi-al-haqq may describe an omitted verbal noun, meaning a recitation characterized by truth and accuracy.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r12.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف وقع صفة لمصدر اتل أى اتل تلاوة متلبسة بالحق

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r13.claim: Alternatively, it is a circumstantial phrase describing the reciter or the account, true and consistent with earlier scriptures.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r13.anchor: أو حال من فاعل اتل أو من مفعوله متلبسا أنت أو نبأهما بالحق

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r14.claim: Idh is a time adverb attached to nabaa; although nabaa is originally a verbal noun, its verbal force permits the time phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r14.anchor: ظرف لنبأ وعمل فيه لأنه مصدر فى الأصل والظرف يكفى فيه رائحة الفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r15.claim: A proposed attachment as a circumstantial phrase from an omitted element is objected to because past idh does not fit the future recite; al-Alusi replies that the two parses differ.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r15.anchor: وجوز أن يكون متعلقا بمحذوف وقع حالا منه ورد بأنه حينئذ

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r16.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r16.claim: Al-Bahr rejects treating idh as a substitute for nabaa with an omitted noun, since idh is added to time expressions, not nabaa; the response says both constructions are semantically and grammatically sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r16.anchor: ورده فى البحر بأن إذ لايضاف اليها إلا الزمان نحو يومئذ وحينئذ

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r17.claim: Qurban means anything offered to draw near to God, including a sacrifice or other gift; it is singular because it is originally a verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r17.anchor: والقربان اسم لما يتقرب به إلى الله تعالى من ذبيحة أو غيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r19.claim: Qabil's offering was rejected because he resented God's ruling that he could not marry his twin sister.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r19.anchor: لأنه سخط حكم الله تعالى وهو عدم جواز نكاح التوأمة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r20.claim: The speech clause resumes the narrative as an implicit question and answer: what did the one whose offering failed say?
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r20.anchor: قال ( استئناف سؤال نشأ من الكلام السابق كأنه قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r21.claim: Qabil's threat arose from envy at Habil's accepted offering and standing with God; another view attributes it to the prospect of losing the beautiful sister.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r21.anchor: لفرط الحسد على قبول قربانه ورفعة شأنه عند ربه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r22.claim: The emphatic final n is recited both geminated and, in a variant reading, lightened.

ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r23.claim: The reply means that God accepts offerings and worship only from the God-fearing, with sincerity directed to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p110#2/r23.anchor: إنما يتقبل الله ( أى القربان والطاعة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r1.claim: Taqwa here means more than the first level of avoiding idolatry; Qabil's rejection resulted from his own abandonment of taqwa, not from Habil, so he should reform himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r1.anchor: وليس المراد من التقوى التقوى من الشرك التى هى أول المراتب

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r2.claim: This is a concise, wise reply that redirects blame to Qabil's own failure to acquire the taqwa that brings acceptance.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r2.anchor: إنك إنما أتيت من قبل نفسك لانسلاخها عن لباس التقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r3.claim: An envier should attribute deprivation to his own shortcomings and seek the qualities that brought another person favor, rather than trying to remove that person's blessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r3.anchor: أن الحاسد ينبغى أن يرى حرمانه من تقصيره ويجتهد فى تحصيل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r4.claim: One interpretation takes Habil to mean that he will not evade God's threatened judgment, since the pious prefer obedience to life; al-Alusi calls this remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r4.anchor: وقيل : مراده الكناية عن أنه لايمتنع عن حكم الله تعالى بوعيده

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r5.claim: A second interpretation says Habil will not kill Qabil in order to prevent being killed; the author also finds this reading remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r5.anchor: أو الكناية عن أنه لايقتله دفعا لقتله لأنه متق

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r6.claim: The verse sternly rebukes people who perform deeds without the taqwa required for acceptance.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r6.anchor: وماأنعى هذه الآية على العاملين أعمالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r7.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r7.claim: At death, ʿAmir ibn ʿAbd Allah wept and explained that he heard God say acceptance is only from the God-fearing.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112/r7.anchor: وعن عامر بن عبد الله أنه بكى حين حضرته الوفاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r1.claim: The two sons of Adam are Habil and Qabil; Qabil is also called Qabin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r1.anchor: نبأ ابني آدم بالحق} وهما هابيل وقابيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r2.speaker: أهل العلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r2.claim: The account says Eve bore one boy and one girl in each of twenty pregnancies, forty children total, from Qabil and his twin Aqlima to ʿAbd al-Mughith and his twin Umm al-Mughith.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r2.anchor: أن حواء كانت تلد لآدم عليه السلام في كل بطن غلاما وجارية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Adam lived until his children and grandchildren numbered forty thousand.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم يمت آدم حتى بلغ ولده وولد ولده أربعين ألفا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r4.claim: One account says Qabil and his twin Aqlima were born a hundred years after Adam and Eve descended to earth, followed by Habil and his twin Labuda.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r4.anchor: فقال بعضهم: غشي آدم حواء بعد مهبطهما إلى الأرض بمائة سنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r5.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq, citing scriptural scholars, says Qabil and Aqlima were conceived in Paradise before the sin without pregnancy pains, while Habil and Labuda were conceived after the descent and accompanied by the pains and blood of childbirth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r5.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق عن بعض أهل العلم بالكتاب الأول: إن آدم كان يغشى حواء في الجنة قبل أن يصيب الخطيئة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r6.claim: Because the only women were their sisters, Adam’s children married a sister from another twin pair, never their own twin; Qabil and Habil were two years apart, according to al-Kalbi.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r6.anchor: يتزوج أية أخواته شاء إلا توأمته التي ولدت معه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r7.claim: God ordered Qabil to marry Habil’s sister Labuda and Habil to marry Qabil’s sister Aqlima; Qabil objected because his twin was more beautiful, while Habil accepted. Adam said the accepted offering would decide who married her.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r7.anchor: أمر الله تعالى آدم عليه السلام أن ينكح قابيل لبودا أخت هابيل وينكح هابيل أقليما أخت قابيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r8.claim: At that time an accepted offering was consumed by white fire from heaven; a rejected offering was left for birds and beasts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r8.anchor: وكانت القرابين إذا كانت مقبولة نزلت نار من السماء بيضاء فأكلتها، وإذا لم تكن مقبولة لم تنزل النار وأكلته الطير والسباع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r9.claim: Qabil, a farmer, offered a pile of his poorest grain and inwardly did not care whether God accepted it; Habil, a shepherd, offered his best ram sincerely seeking God’s approval. Fire consumed Habil’s offering alone.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r9.anchor: وكان قابيل صاحب زرع فقرب صبرة من الطعام من أردأ زرعه وأضمر في نفسه ما أبالي أيقبل مني أم لا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r10.claim: The accepted brother is Habil and the rejected one Qabil.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r11.claim: After his offering was rejected, Qabil nursed envy; when Adam left to visit the House in Mecca, Qabil approached Habil among the flock and threatened him, resentful of Habil’s accepted offering and better marriage.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r11.anchor: فلما غاب آدم أتى قابيل هابيل وهو في غنمه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r12.claim: Qabil explains his threat by saying God accepted Habil’s offering, rejected his, gave Habil the beautiful sister, and left him the plain one, so people and their descendants would consider Habil superior.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r12.anchor: لأن الله تعالى قبل قربانك ورد قرباني، وتنكح أختي الحسناء وأنكح أختك الدميمة، فيتحدث الناس أنك خير مني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r13.claim: Habil answers that he bears no guilt for Qabil’s rejection and that God accepts only from the God-fearing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p41/r13.anchor: {قال} هابيل: وما ذنبي؟ {إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين}

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r1.claim: The two sons are Cain and Abel; God directed Adam to marry each to the other’s twin, but Cain resented that his twin was more beautiful. Adam told them to offer sacrifices, and the accepted offering was Abel’s, consumed by fire, increasing Cain’s anger.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r1.anchor: قابيل وهابيل، أوحى الله سبحانه وتعالى إلى آدم أن يزوج كل واحد منهما توأمة الآخر، فسخط منه قابيل لأن توأمته كانت أجمل، فقال لهما آدم: قربا قربانا فمن أيكما قبل تزوجها، فقبل قربان هابيل بأن نزلت نار فأكلته، فازداد قابيل سخطا وفعل ما فعل

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r2.claim: Another view says they were two Israelite men rather than Adam’s own sons, supported by the following mention of what God prescribed for Israel.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r2.anchor: وقيل لم يرد لهما ابني آدم لصلبه وأنهما رجلان

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r3.claim: “In truth” may qualify an omitted verbal noun, be circumstantial with “recite,” or qualify the account itself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r3.anchor: صفة مصدر محذوف أي تلاوة ملتبسة بالحق، أو حال من الضمير في اتل، أو من نبأ

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r4.claim: The account is truthful and agrees with the earlier scriptures.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r4.anchor: ملتبسا بالصدق موافقا لما في كتب الأولين

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r5.claim: Idh may be temporal to nabāʾ, circumstantial, or an apposition with an omitted genitive: the account of that time.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r5.anchor: ظرف لنبأ، أو حال منه، أو بدل على حذف مضاف أي واتل عليهم نبأهما نبأ ذلك الوقت

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r6.claim: Qurbān is an offering by which one draws near to God, slaughter or otherwise; originally a verbal noun, it does not take a dual, though one may understand that each offered an offering.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r6.anchor: والقربان اسم ما يتقرب به إلى الله سبحانه وتعالى من ذبيحة أو غيرها، كما أن الحلوان اسم ما يحلى به أي يعطى، وهو في الأصل مصدر ولذلك لم يثن وقيل تقديره إذ قرب كل واحد منهما قربانا

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r7.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r7.claim: One report says Cain was a farmer and offered his worst wheat, while Abel was a herdsman and offered a fat camel.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27/r7.anchor: قيل كان قابيل صاحب زرع وقرب أردأ قمح عنه، وهابيل صاحب ضرع وقرب جملا سمينا

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r1.claim: Cain’s offering was rejected because he resented God’s judgment, lacked sincerity, and chose the worst of what he had.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r1.anchor: لأنه سخط حكم الله سبحانه وتعالى ولم يخلص النية في قربانه وقصد إلى أخس ما عنده

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r2.claim: Cain threatened Abel because envy consumed him when Abel’s offering was accepted.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r2.anchor: توعده بالقتل لفرط الحسد له على تقبل قربانه

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r3.claim: Abel replies that Cain’s own lack of piety caused his deprivation; an envious person should work to acquire the quality that blessed the envied person, not try to remove that blessing, and obedience is accepted only from a believing, God-fearing person.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r3.anchor: أي إنما أتيت من قبل نفسك بترك التقوى لا من قبلي فلم تقتلني، وفيه إشارة إلى أن الحاسد ينبغي أن يرى حرمانه من تقصيره ويجتهد في تحصيل ما به صار المحسود محظوظا، لا في إزالة حظه فإن ذلك مما يضره ولا ينفعه، وأن الطاعة لا تقبل إلا من مؤمن متق

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r1.claim: After the Israelites' breach of the Holy Land covenant and punishment, this story refutes Jewish divine-sonship claims, which also defeats the Christian claim through their ancestry.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r1.anchor: في أمرهم بالدخول إلى الأرض المقدسة لما فيها من نقض العهود

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r2.claim: The command addresses the people being called, including Jews; reciting this story is a major proof of the Prophet's mission because only revelation could give him and his people this knowledge.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r3.claim: The account is true because it agrees with what actually happened and is found in the books of earlier peoples.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r3.anchor: أي الخبر الذي يطابقه الواقع إذا تعرف من كتب الأولين

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r4.claim: نبأ marks the consequential, weighty account of Adam's two sons.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r4.anchor: أي خبرهما الجليل العظيم , تلاوة ملتبسة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r5.claim: Each son offered something meant to bring him as close as possible to the desired object; the kind of offering is irrelevant to the point here.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r5.anchor: ولما لم يتعلق الغرض في هذا المقام ببيان أي نوع قربا منه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r6.claim: Acceptance is passive because the key issue is one offering's rejection, not identifying who accepted it; the acceptance was publicly apparent.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r6.anchor: المؤثر للحسد إنما هو عدم التقبل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r7.claim: The accepted son is left unnamed because identifying him is unnecessary to the point of the passage.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r7.anchor: أبهمه أيضا لعدم الاحتياج في هذا السياق إلى تعيينه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r8.claim: The brothers knew acceptance by a sign, perhaps fire consuming the accepted offering as people say, or by some other indication.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r8.anchor: إما أكل النار للمقبول كما قالوه أو غير ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r9.speaker: قيل
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r9.claim: Some say Cain was born in Paradise; despite this closeness to Adam, he was punished for breaking the covenant, undermining claims to inherited divine favor.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r9.anchor: ولد في الجنة على ما قيل , ومع ذلك فقد عذب

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r10.claim: The brothers shared one law, and reward or punishment depended on loyalty or breach: the loyal is God's beloved ally, the covenant-breaker His hated enemy, regardless of descent.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r11.claim: If even Adam's direct son, reportedly born in Paradise, was not exempt from punishment or loss of divine love, those more remote have still less basis to claim filial privilege.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r11.anchor: مع كونه لصلبه لا واسطة بينهما ومع كونه ولد في الجنة دار الكرامة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r12.claim: The story warns the Jews that envy in their rejection of Muhammad leads to deeds rejected by God and reason and ends in the Fire.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r12.anchor: كفر بني إسرائيل بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما هو للحسد

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r13.claim: Israel held back from fighting distant enemies despite command and promised reward, while Cain advanced to kill his beloved, forbidden-to-kill brother; this teaches the community in both action and restraint and recalls God's protection from such conduct.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r13.anchor: في قصة بني إسرائيل إحجامهم عن قتال أعداء الله البعداء منهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r14.claim: Moses and Aaron were exceptionally obedient, compassionate brothers, in contrast to Cain and Abel; the contrast warns against the envy that led to Cain's act.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r14.anchor: أن موسى وهارون عليهما السلام أخوان في غاية الطواعية

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r15.claim: Israel's prophet inferred that their spoils were not accepted when the fire failed to consume them because of embezzlement; after the embezzled item was recovered, the fire consumed it, paralleling the brothers' offerings.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r16.claim: The Israelites were punished by being barred from Jerusalem and made to wander, while Cain was expelled from the land where his brother was killed.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r16.anchor: وقابيل نفي من الأرض التي كان فيها مقتل أخيه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r17.claim: Al-Baghawi transmits from Ibn Abbas that Cain wandered forty days carrying Abel on his back as beasts pursued him; the author compares this with Israel's forty-year wandering and the days their scouts investigated the giants.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r17.anchor: ذكره البغوي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال

BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r18.claim: The author calls the preceding parallels enhancements, then proposes a stronger coherence: link the command to recite with Moses' earlier prohibition on grieving and the promise of the Holy Land to Israel.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p442/r18.anchor: وأحسن منه أن يكون الأمر لموسى عليه السلام عطفا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r1.claim: The Holy Land was promised to Israel's descendants although Moses would die before entering it; since settled people envy and turn against each other, Moses is to recite the story as a warning after they defeat the giants and prosper in the land.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r1.anchor: فأنا مورثها لا محالة لأبنائهم وأنت متوف قبل دخولها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r2.claim: The story also warns the Muslim community after completion of its religion and the Prophet's death: conquest, wealth, and comfort can make people forget hardship, repeat earlier nations' acts, and disregard punishment's dangers.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r2.anchor: وعظا لهذه الأمة ومانعا من فعل مثل ذلك بعد إكمال دينهم ووفاة نبيهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r3.claim: The Prophet says the disease of earlier nations has entered this community: envy and hatred, with hatred cutting away religion rather than hair. Al-Mundhiri calls its chain good; it is also cited from al-Tirmidhi, Ahmad, al-Tayalisi, al-Bazzar, and al-Bayhaqi.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r3.anchor: كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( دب إليكم داء الأمم قبلكم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet says people remain in a good state as long as they do not envy; al-Tabarani transmits it with trustworthy narrators.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r4.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r5.speaker: عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r5.claim: Al-Kala'i recounts that when Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas sent spoils, Umar refused to store them under a roof before division; after guarding the mosque courtyard, Ibn Awf and Ibn Arqam uncovered its jewels, and Umar said wealth brings envy, hatred, and conflict among its recipients.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r5.anchor: فقال عمر : والله ما ذاك يبكيني

BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r6.speaker: المترجم
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r6.claim: The cited Torah translation says Adam named Eve because she was mother of every living being, God clothed them in skins and sent them from Eden to till the earth, and Adam joined with her and she bore Cain.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p443/r6.anchor: قال المترجم في أولها بعد قصة أكل آدم عليه السلام من الشجرة ما نصه : فدعا آدم اسم امرأته حواء

BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r2.claim: After one offering is rejected and the other accepted, Cain’s anger and envy lead him to threaten his brother with murder.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r2.anchor: أي لأخيه الذي قبل قربانه حسدا له

BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r3.claim: Only those deeply characterized by piety are accepted; they do not persist in sins, whether idolatry or otherwise.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r3.anchor: فلا معصية لهم يصرون عليها بشرك ولا غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r4.claim: The rejected offering reflects Cain’s own state, not Abel’s; killing Abel only distances Cain further from the rank he envies.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r4.anchor: فعدم تقبل قربانك من نفسك لا مني

DURR-FULL:v3p54/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r1.speaker: ناس من الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r1.claim: A report from some Companions says Adam's children were born as male-female twins who married across birth cohorts; Cain wanted the more beautiful twin born with him, but Adam directed Abel to marry her and Cain refused.
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود عن ناس من الصحابة أنه كان لايولد لآدم مولود ألا ولد معه جارية

DURR-FULL:v3p54/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r2.speaker: ناس من الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r2.claim: In that report, Adam entrusted his household to heaven, earth, and mountains as he went to Mecca; Cain accepted the trust, then Abel offered a fat yearling while Cain offered grain, and fire consumed Abel's offering alone.
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r2.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن ابن مسعود عن ناس من الصحابة

DURR-FULL:v3p54/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r3.speaker: ناس من الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r3.claim: Cain threatened Abel over the marriage; Abel answered that God accepts only from the God-fearing and wanted Cain to bear the sin of killing him together with his own existing sin.
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r3.anchor: فغضب وقال: لأقتلنك حتى لا تنكح أختي فقال هابيل {إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين}

DURR-FULL:v3p54/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says marriage to one's twin sister or another sister was forbidden; after a dispute over a beautiful and an ugly twin, the brothers offered a white ram and grain, God accepted the ram and kept it in Paradise for forty years as Abraham's sacrificial ram, and humanity descends from the unbelieving brother.
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نهى أن ينكح المرأة أخاها توأمها وأن ينكحها غيره من اخوتها

DURR-FULL:v3p55/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r1.claim: Via al-Dahhak, Ibn Abbas says Adam had forty children, twenty sons and twenty daughters, including the named surviving children; God ordered siblings paired across families in marriage.
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: ولد لآدم أربعون ولدا عشرون غلاما وعشرون جارية

DURR-FULL:v3p55/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says offerings were made before there were poor people to receive charity: a shepherd offered his best sheep and a farmer some crops; fire accepted the sheep, and Cain threatened Abel because people knew whose offering was rejected.
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان من شأن ابني آدم أنه لم يكن مسكين يتصدق عليه

DURR-FULL:v3p55/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r3.claim: Ibn Umar contrasts the shepherd's best, willingly offered sheep with the farmer's inferior, reluctantly offered crop; God accepted the former, and the murdered brother was stronger but held back by scrupulous fear.
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: إن ابني آدم اللذين قربا قربانا كان أحدهما صاحب حرث

DURR-FULL:v3p55/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r4.claim: Mujahid identifies the two sons as Habil and Qabil, sons of Adam himself; Abel offered a fine she-goat from his flock, Cain offered crops, and God accepted the sheep, prompting Cain's threat to kill him.
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم} قال: هابيل وقابيل

DURR-FULL:v3p56/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r1.claim: Mujahid's account continues: after Cain killed Abel, God bound one of Cain's legs to his thigh; he faced south, endured alternating snow in winter and fire in summer, and was attended by seven angels in rotation.
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r1.anchor: فقتله فعقل الله إحدى رجليه بساقه إلى فخذها من يوم قتله إلى يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v3p56/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r2.claim: Al-Hasan rejects the view that these were Adam's biological sons: they were Israelites, and the offering story occurred among the Children of Israel; one was the first person to die.
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r2.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق} قال: كانا من بني إسرائيل

DURR-FULL:v3p56/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r3.claim: Abu al-Darda says certainty that God accepted even one prayer would be dearer to him than the whole world.
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r3.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: لأن استيقن ان الله

DURR-FULL:v3p56/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r4.claim: Ali says no action is small when accompanied by piety, since what God accepts cannot be considered small.
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r4.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: لايقل عمل مع تقوى

DURR-FULL:v3p56/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r5.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r5.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz writes that God accepts, shows mercy, and rewards only on the basis of piety; preachers of piety are many but practitioners few.
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r5.anchor: عن عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه كتب إلى رجل: أوصيك بتقوى الله الذي لايقبل غيرها

DURR-FULL:v3p56/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r6.speaker: موسى بن أعين
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r6.claim: Musa ibn A'yan explains the God-fearing as people who avoid some lawful things lest they fall into what is forbidden.
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r6.anchor: سألت موسى بن أعين عن قوله عز وجل

DURR-FULL:v3p56/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r7.speaker: فضالة بن عبيد
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r7.claim: Fadala ibn Ubayd says knowing that God accepted a mustard seed's worth of one's deed would be dearer than the world.
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r7.anchor: عن فضالة بن عبيد قال: لأن أكون اعلم أن الله يقبل مني مثقال حبة

DURR-FULL:v3p56/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r8.speaker: عامر بن عبد قيس
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r8.claim: Amir ibn Abd Qays says being made one of the God-fearing, as this verse promises, would be worth more than the whole world.
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r8.anchor: عن قتادة قال: قال عامر بن عبد قيس آية في القرآن أحب إلي

DURR-FULL:v3p56/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r9.speaker: همام بن يحيى
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r9.claim: Hammam ibn Yahya recounts that Amir ibn Abdullah wept at death and said he feared the verse that limits acceptance to the God-fearing.
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r9.anchor: عن همام بن يحيى قال: بكى عامر بن عبد الله عند الموت

DURR-FULL:v3p56/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r10.claim: Al-Hasan transmits that the Prophet said God does not accept a servant's deed until He is pleased with the servant.
DURR-FULL:v3p56/r10.anchor: عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله لايقبل عمل عبد

DURR-FULL:v3p57/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r1.speaker: مطرف
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r1.claim: Thabit says Mutarrif would ask God to accept a day's fast and record a good deed, then recite the verse about acceptance and piety.
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r1.anchor: عن ثابت قال: كان مطرف يقول: اللهم تقبل مني صيام يوم

DURR-FULL:v3p57/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r2.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak defines the God-fearing here as those who avoid associating partners with God.
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين} قال: الذين يتقون الشرك

DURR-FULL:v3p57/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r3.claim: Ibn Umar gave a beggar a dinar; when his son prayed for its acceptance, Ibn Umar said certainty about one accepted prostration or dirham would make death more welcome, for God accepts only from the God-fearing.
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r3.anchor: عن هشام بن يحيى عن أبيه قال: دخل سائل إلى ابن عمر فقال لابنه: اعطه دينار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r1.claim: “The two sons of Adam” means his two sons; “son of Adam” in the singular can mean one human being, while the plural can address humanity collectively.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r1.anchor: ومعنى { ابني آدم } هنا ولداه . وأما ابن آدم مفردا فقد يراد به واحد من البشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r2.claim: Bi-l-ḥaqq may mean truthfully and accurately: truth is established reality, unlike falsehood, as in the account of the youths of the cave.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r2.anchor: والمراد من الحق هنا الصدق من حق الشيء إذا ثبت ، والصدق هو الثابت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r3.claim: Alternatively, “with truth” can mean seriously and not as amusement, so the account should be recited with a proper purpose rather than for entertainment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r3.anchor: ويصح أن يكون الحق ضد الباطل وهو الجد غير الهزل ، أي اتل هذا النبأ متلبسا بالحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r4.claim: The phrase may also warn against Israelite storytellers’ additions to the reasons one brother killed the other.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p168/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون قوله { بالحق } مشيرا إلى ما خف بالقصة من زيادات زادها أهل القصص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r1.claim: Idh is a temporal adverb attached to nabāʾ, locating the account at the time the two offered their sacrifices.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r1.anchor: أي خبرهما الحاصل وقت تقريبهما قربانا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r2.claim: Qarrabā derives from qurbān, now a lexicalized noun originally meaning what one offers to God, such as charity, sacrifice, or prayer; it does not mean simply “brought near.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r2.anchor: وفعل { قربا } هنا مشتق من القربان الذي صار بمنزلة الاسم الجامد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r3.claim: The Torah names the brothers Cain and Abel, called Qabil and Habil in Arabic; Qabil farmed, while Habil herded sheep, and they offered crops and firstborn flock respectively.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r3.anchor: وفي التوراة هما ( قايين ) والعرب يسمونه قابيل وأخوه ( هابيل )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAshur says it is unknown whether offerings were distributed to the poor or left for people generally.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r4.anchor: ولا ندري هل كان القربان عندهم يعطى للفقراء ونحوهم أو كان يترك للناس عامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r5.claim: God accepted Habil’s offering, not Qabil’s; apparently God revealed that outcome to Adam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r5.anchor: فتقبل الله قربان هابيل ولم يتقبل قربان قابيل . والظاهر أن قبول قربان أحدهما دون الآخر حصل بوحي من الله لآدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r6.claim: God rejected Qabil’s offering because he was not righteous and had sins.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r6.anchor: وإنما لم يتقبل الله قربان قابيل لأنه لم يكن رجلا صالحا بل كانت له خطايا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r7.claim: An alternative says Qabil was an unbeliever; Ibn ʿAshur rejects this because it conflicts with his making an offering.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r7.anchor: وقيل : كان كافرا ، وهذا ينافي كونه يقرب قربانا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r8.claim: The singular qurbān is generic: each brother made his own offering, rather than the two sharing one sacrifice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r8.anchor: وأفرد القربان في الآية لإرادة الجنس ، وإنما قرب كل واحد منهما قربانا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r9.claim: God does not name which brother’s offering was accepted because identification adds nothing to the lesson.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r9.anchor: ولم يسم الله تعالى المتقبل منه والذي لم يتقبل منه إذ لا جدوى لذلك في موقع العبرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r10.claim: Jealousy over the distinction of acceptance drove the murder; envy was the first crime to appear on earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r10.anchor: وإنما حمله على قتل أخيه حسده على مزية القبول . والحسد أول جريمة ظهرت في الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r11.claim: Habil’s reply is admonition and a disclaimer of any cause for murder: acceptance belongs to God and comes from the God-fearing, implicitly showing his brother was not pious and that the accepted offering gives no grounds for killing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r11.anchor: وقوله في الجواب { إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين } موعظة وتعريض وتنصل مما يوجب قتله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r12.claim: If muttaqūn has its ordinary religious sense, the claim restricts acceptance to the pious; that may have been their law, later superseded by Islam’s acceptance of a believer’s good deeds despite other lapses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r12.anchor: فإذا كان المراد من المتقين معناه المعروف شرعا المحكي بلفظه الدال عليه مراد ابن آدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r13.claim: Another reading takes “pious” to mean sincere in the act, making nonacceptance evidence of insincerity; Ibn ʿAshur says this stretches the customary meaning of taqwa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r13.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد بالمتقين المخلصون في العمل ، فيكون عدم القبول أمارة على عدم الإخلاص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r14.claim: A third reading understands acceptance as complete acceptance, indicated by a sacrifice being consumed by fire, like complete guidance for the pious and the full afterlife reserved for them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r14.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد بالتقبل تقبلا خاصا ، وهو التقبل التام الدال عليه احتراق القربان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r15.claim: A further possibility is that the restriction concerns acceptance of sacrifices specifically.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r15.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد تقبل القرابين خاصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r16.claim: Alternatively, piety means intending God-consciousness through the offering; Habil’s brother instead intended to boast, and acceptance in that sense was the law of their time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p169/r16.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد المتقين بالقربان ، أي المريدين به تقوى الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r1.claim: Atlu means narrate and make them hear; naba' means a report.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r1.anchor: اتل معناه اسرد وأسمعهم إياه، وهذه من علوم الكتب الأول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r2.claim: The story is knowledge from earlier scriptures, inaccessible to Muhammad except by revelation, so it is evidence of his prophethood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r2.anchor: لا تعلق لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بها إلا من طريق الوحي، فهو من دلائل نبوته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r3.claim: The pronoun most likely addresses the Children of Israel: the preceding argument addresses them, and the obscure story was known from their scriptures, making its telling a proof against them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r3.anchor: والضمير في عليهم ظاهر أمره أنه يراد به بنو إسرائيل لوجهين: أحدهما أن المحاورة فيما تقدم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r4.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r4.claim: The majority of exegetes identify the two sons as Cain and Abel, biological sons of Adam.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r4.anchor: و «ابنا آدم» هما في قول جمهور المفسرين لصلبه. وهما قابيل وهابيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r5.speaker: الحسن البصري
