IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r5.claim: Hasan al-Basri says they were not Adam's biological sons and that sacrifices occurred only among the Israelites; Ibn Atiyya calls this mistaken because Israelites would not be ignorant of burial until the crow taught them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن البصري «ابنا آدم» ليسا لصلبه ولم تكن القرابين إلا في بني إسرائيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r6.claim: A report says the brothers made their offerings as voluntary devotion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r6.anchor: وروي أن تقريبهما للقربان إنما كان تحنثا وتطوعا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r7.claim: Cain, a farmer, offered his worst produce, while Abel, a shepherd, offered his best ram; their custom was to pray after offering, and a descending fire signaled acceptance, taking Abel's ram and leaving Cain's crop.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r7.anchor: وكان قابيل صاحب زرع فعمد إلى أرذل ما عنده وأدناه فقربه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r8.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others say Abel's ram grazed in Paradise until it was sent down to Abraham as the ransom for his son.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r8.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير وغيره: فكان ذلك الكبش يرتع في الجنة حتى أهبط إلى إبراهيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r9.speaker: سائقو هذا القصص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r9.claim: Storytellers say Cain envied Abel and resented that people regarded Abel as better; Cain was Adam's eldest son.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r9.anchor: فحسد قابيل هابيل وقال له: أتمشي على الأرض يراك الناس أفضل مني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r10.claim: A report says Adam travelled to Mecca to see the Ka'ba, left Cain overseeing his children, and the episode occurred during his absence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r10.anchor: وروي أن «آدم» سافر إلى مكة ليرى الكعبة وترك قابيل وصيا على بنيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود وجماعة من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r11.claim: A report says Eve bore a boy and girl in each pregnancy; Adam arranged cross-twin marriages, but Cain wanted his own attractive twin sister, disobeyed Adam, and the brothers agreed to offer sacrifices.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r11.anchor: وروت جماعة من المفسرين منهم ابن مسعود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r12.claim: Another report says Adam witnessed the offerings; Abel's acceptance meant Cain had to accept the other marriage match, after which Cain threatened him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r12.anchor: وروي أن آدم حضر ذلك فتقبل قربان هابيل ووجب أن يأخذ أخت قابيل، فحينئذ قال له لأقتلنك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r13.claim: Abel's reply has an omitted preceding question: why kill me when I am guiltless of your rejected offering? I feared God and followed truth; God accepts only the Godfearing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178/r13.anchor: وقول هابيل: إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين كلام قبله محذوف تقديره ولم تقتلني وأنا لم أجن شيئا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r1.speaker: أهل السنة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r1.claim: Ahl al-Sunna agree that taqwa here means avoiding shirk: a monotheist whose sincere works are genuine has them accepted; avoiding both shirk and sins brings the highest degree of acceptance and assured mercy, known through God's reports rather than rational obligation upon Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق: وإجماع أهل السنة في معنى هذه الألفاظ أنها اتقاء الشرك، فمن اتقاه وهو موحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r2.speaker: عدي بن ثابت وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r2.claim: Adi ibn Thabit and others say the offering of this community's Godfearing people is prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r2.anchor: وقال عدي بن ثابت وغيره: قربان متقي هذه الأمة الصلاة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r1.claim: Al-nabaʾ means a report or news.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r2.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r2.claim: Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada say the two were Adam's own sons, Cain and Abel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنهما ابناه لصلبه وهما قابيل وهابيل قاله ابن عمر وابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says they were two brothers from the Children of Israel, not Adam's own sons.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r3.anchor: والثاني أنها أخوان من بني إسرائيل ولم يكونا ابني آدم لصلبه هذا قول الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r4.claim: The author prefers that they were Adam's own sons: the next verse describes one showing the other how to bury his brother, and the Prophet called him the first to institute murder.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r5.claim: The account is to be recited truthfully, as it happened.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r5.anchor: أي كما كان والقربان فعلان من القرب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r6.claim: Qurban is on the faʿlan pattern from the root meaning nearness; Ibn al-Jawzi says he discussed it in Al Imran.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r6.anchor: والقربان فعلان من القرب وقد ذكرناه في آل عمران

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas's account says Adam forbade marrying a twin sister but allowed another sister; after disputes over paired daughters, the farmer and herder offered to decide the match. Abel's ram was accepted over Cain's grain, kept in Paradise forty years, and was Abraham's sacrifice; Cain then killed Abel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r7.anchor: رواه سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r8.claim: Al-Awfi reports from Ibn Abbas that the brothers spontaneously decided to offer: fire consumed Abel's best sheep but left Cain's produce, prompting his threat.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r8.anchor: روى العوفي عن ابن عباس أن ابني آدم كانا قاعدين يوما فقالا لو قربنا قربانا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r9.claim: The commentators differ over whether Cain and his sister were born before or after Abel and his sister.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r9.anchor: واختلفوا هل قابيل وأخته ولدا قبل هابيل وأخته أم بعدهما على قولين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r10.claim: One view places Cain and his sister's birth before Abel and his sister's.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r10.anchor: هل قابيل وأخته ولدا قبل هابيل وأخته أم بعدهما على قولين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r11.claim: The alternative view places Cain and his sister's birth after Abel and his sister's.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r11.anchor: ولدا قبل هابيل وأخته أم بعدهما على قولين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r12.claim: The commentators also differ over whether Cain was an unbeliever or a sinner who was not an unbeliever.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r12.anchor: وهل كان قابيل كافرا أو فاسقا غير كافر فيه قولان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r13.claim: One view calls Cain an unbeliever.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r13.anchor: وهل كان قابيل كافرا أو فاسقا غير كافر فيه قولان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r14.claim: The alternative view calls Cain sinful but not an unbeliever.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p331/r14.anchor: أو فاسقا غير كافر فيه قولان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r1.claim: One explanation for Abel's accepted offering is that he was more God-fearing than Cain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنه كان أتقى لله من قابيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r2.claim: Another explanation is that Abel offered the best of his property while Cain offered the worst.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه تقرب بخيار ماله وتقرب قابيل بشر ماله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r3.claim: One view says the offerings were made while Adam had gone to visit the Sacred House.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r3.anchor: أحدهما أنه كان وآدم قد ذهب إلى زيارة البيت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r4.claim: Another view says Adam ordered the brothers to make offerings.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r5.claim: One view says Cain killed Abel before the sister's marriage to prevent her being given to Abel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r5.anchor: أحدهما أنه قتله قبل ذلك لئلا يصل إليها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r6.claim: Another view says Cain killed Abel after the sister had married.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r7.speaker: يعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r7.claim: Ya'qub, as transmitted by Zayd, reads the emphatic nun with sukūn and lightens it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r7.anchor: وروى زيد عن يعقوب لأقتلنك بسكون النون وتخفيفها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r8.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r8.claim: The threat's speaker is the brother whose offering was rejected; al-Farra' says context makes the omitted name clear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r8.anchor: والقائل هو الذي لم يتقبل منه قال الفراء إنما حذف ذكره لأن المعنى يدل عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the God-fearing meant here are those who avoid sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r9.anchor: أحدهما أنهم الذين يتقون المعاصي قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r10.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says the God-fearing meant here are those who avoid associating partners with God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p333/r10.anchor: والثاني أنهم الذين يتقون الشرك قاله الضحاك

MUSNAD-AHMAD:24103/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:24103/r1.speaker: عائشة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:24103/r1.claim: Aisha recalls that during his illness the Prophet obtained his wives' permission to stay with her, then entered supported by al-Abbas and Ali, his feet dragging; Ibn Abbas identifies Ali as the second man.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:24103/r1.anchor: عن عائشة، قال: سفيان سمعت منه حديثا طويلا ليس أحفظ (1) من أوله إلا قليلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr presents the murder as the ruinous outcome of envy and oppression: the victim gained by having his burden placed on Cain and entering Paradise, while the killer lost in this life and the next.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r1.anchor: كيف عدا أحدهما على الآخر، فقتله بغيا عليه وحسدا له، فيما وهبه الله من النعمة وتقبل القربان الذي أخلص فيه لله عز وجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r2.claim: According to the majority, these were Adam's own sons, Hābil and Qābil; Ibn Kathīr says earlier and later authorities also identify them by those names.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r2.anchor: آدم لصلبه -في قول الجمهور-وهما هابيل وقابيل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r3.claim: Here bil-ḥaqq means a clear account free of ambiguity, lies, error, alteration, addition, or omission.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r3.anchor: {بالحق} أي: على الجلية والأمر الذي لا لبس فيه ولا كذب، ولا وهم ولا تبديل، ولا زيادة ولا نقصان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr compares this description of the account with Qur'anic declarations that other narratives are the true account or are told in truth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r4.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {إن هذا لهو القصص الحق} [آل عمران:62] وقال تعالى: {نحن نقص عليك نبأهم بالحق}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r5.claim: He also links the wording to the declaration that Jesus son of Mary is the word of truth about which people dispute.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r5.anchor: وقال تعالى: {ذلك عيسى ابن مريم قول الحق الذي فيه يمترون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr addresses the account to envious aggressors, polemically identifying the Jews and their likes as kin of apes and pigs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r6.anchor: واقصص على هؤلاء البغاة الحسدة، إخوان الخنازير والقردة من اليهود وأمثالهم وأشباههم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r7.speaker: غير واحد من السلف والخلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r7.claim: One account says God permitted Adam, from necessity, to marry daughters to sons, pairing children from different twin births; Qābil wanted his own beautiful twin, so Adam made the accepted offering decide whom she would marry.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p81/r7.anchor: فيما ذكره غير واحد من السلف والخلف، أن الله تعالى قد شرع لآدم، عليه السلام، أن يزوج بناته من بنيه لضرورة الحال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p82/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p82/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p82/r1.claim: Al-Suddī reports that Adam paired male and female twins across births; Qābil coveted his beautiful twin and argued he had the stronger claim because he was older and his father's successor.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p82/r1.anchor: قال السدي -فيما ذكر-عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p82/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p82/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p82/r2.claim: In al-Suddī's account, Adam went to Mecca after being told of God's House and entrusted his family to Qābil; Hābil offered a fine sheep, Qābil grain, and fire consumed Hābil's offering alone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p82/r2.anchor: قال السدي -فيما ذكر-عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p82/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p82/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p82/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a woman could not marry her twin brother and was paired with another brother; the ugly twin's brother wanted the beautiful twin, and the sheep offering was accepted over the crop offering. Ibn Kathīr grades the chain good.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p82/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نهي أن تنكح المرأة أخاها توأمها، وأمر أن ينكحها غيره من إخوتها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Hābil offered a white, horned sheep and Qābil a heap of grain; God accepted and kept the ram in Paradise for forty years, and it was the ram sacrificed by Abraham. Ibn Kathīr calls the chain good.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، قوله {إذ قربا قربانا} فقربا قربانهما، فجاء صاحب الغنم بكبش أعين أقرن أبيض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr says the shepherd offered his best, fattest sheep willingly while the farmer offered spoiled grain unwillingly; the accepted sacrifice led to the quarrel, and the murdered brother was stronger but restrained by scruple.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r2.anchor: عن أبي المغيرة، عن عبد الله بن عمرو (4) قال: إن ابني آدم اللذين قربا قربانا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r3.speaker: إسماعيل بن رافع المدني القاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r3.claim: Ismāʿīl b. Rāfiʿ says he heard that Hābil loved a lamb born in his flock, offered it to God, and it grazed in Paradise until it became the ransom for Abraham's son.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r3.anchor: وقال إسماعيل بن رافع المدني القاص: بلغني أن ابني آدم لما أمرا بالقربان، كان أحدهما صاحب غنم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r4.speaker: محمد بن علي بن الحسين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r4.claim: A report from Adam says he expected a sacrifice in his descendants and asked his sons to offer one; Hābil gave his best sheep, Qābil inferior produce, and fire took Hābil's offering, which Qābil blamed on Adam's prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r4.anchor: حدثنا القاسم بن عبد الرحمن، حدثنا محمد بن علي بن الحسين قال: قال آدم، عليه السلام، لهابيل وقابيل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p84/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p84/r1.speaker: بعض أهل العلم بالكتاب الأول
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p84/r1.claim: Ibn Isḥāq, citing unnamed experts on earlier scripture, says Qābil rejected Adam's cross-twin marriage arrangement, claiming superiority and wanting his beautiful twin; he offered grain against Hābil's prime sheep (some say a cow), and fire accepted Hābil's.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p84/r1.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق، عن بعض أهل العلم بالكتاب الأول: إن آدم أمر ابنه قينا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p84/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p84/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p84/r2.claim: Al-ʿAwfī's report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the sacrifice was a ritual offering, not charity to a poor person, and describes Hābil's best sheep being accepted over Qābil's crop.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p84/r2.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس قال: كان من شأنهما أنه لم يكن مسكين يتصدق عليه، وإنما كان القربان يقربه الرجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p84/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p84/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p84/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr prefers the Qur'an's apparent account: the offering was not prompted by a dispute over a woman; Qābil became angry and envious because Hābil's sacrifice was accepted and his was rejected.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p84/r3.anchor: فهذا الأثر يقتضي أن تقريب القربان كان لا عن سبب ولا عن تدارئ في امرأة، كما تقدم عن جماعة من تقدم ذكرهم، وهو ظاهر القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r1.claim: The majority say Abel offered a sheep and Cain produce; Abel’s offering was accepted and Cain’s was not, a view also well known from Mujahid.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r1.anchor: المشهور عند الجمهور أن الذي قرب الشاة هو هابيل، وأن الذي قرب الطعام هو قابيل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and others identify Abel’s accepted offering as the ram sacrificed in ransom of the one to be slaughtered.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r2.anchor: حتى قال ابن عباس وغيره: إنه الكبش الذي فدي به الذبيح، وهو مناسب، والله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir considers the identification of Abel’s offering as the ram sacrificed in ransom of the one to be slaughtered fitting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r3.anchor: إنه الكبش الذي فدي به الذبيح، وهو مناسب، والله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir reports Mujahid as saying Cain offered produce and was the one whose offering was accepted, contrary to the famous view; Ibn Kathir suspects this was not preserved accurately from him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r4.anchor: ولكن روى ابن جرير، عنه أنه قال: الذي قرب الزرع قابيل، وهو المتقبل منه، وهذا خلاف المشهور،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r5.claim: God accepts only from someone who fears Him in the deed being performed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r5.anchor: ومعنى (1) قوله: {إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين} أي: ممن اتقى الله في فعله ذلك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r6.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r6.claim: Abu al-Darda says certainty that God accepted one prayer would be dearer to him than the world and all it contains, citing this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r6.anchor: عن تميم، يعني ابن مالك المقري، قال: سمعت أبا الدرداء يقول: لأن أستيقن أن الله قد تقبل مني صلاة واحدة أحب إلي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r7.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r7.claim: Abu Afif reports Muadh describing the Godfearing as those who avoid associating partners and idol worship, worship sincerely, and are admitted to Paradise under the Merciful’s protection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85/r7.anchor: فقال له شقيق بن سلمة: يا أبا عفيف، ألا تحدثنا عن معاذ بن جبل؟ قال: بلى، سمعته يقول:

JISHUMI:v3p1932/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r2.claim: Tilāwa means recitation, but its root sense is following: one may say تلوت الرجل تلوا, I followed the man.
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r2.anchor: التلاوة: تلوت القرآن تلاوة، وتلوت الرجل تلوا: تبعته، وهو الأصل في الباب

JISHUMI:v3p1932/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r3.claim: A qurban is an offering used to draw near to God; a king's qurabān are visitors seeking nearness to him, and the word is on the pattern فعْلان from قرب.
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r3.anchor: والقربان: ما يتقرب به إلى الله تعالى، وقربان الملك وقرابينه: زواره

JISHUMI:v3p1932/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r4.claim: The root first denotes nearness in place and then extends to nearness in rank; قربان follows the pattern of عدوان, فرقان, سكران, and كفران.
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r4.anchor: والقربان وزنه فعلان، من القرب، كالعدوان من العدو، والفرقان من الفرق

JISHUMI:v3p1932/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r6.speaker: علي بن عيسى
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r6.claim: Ali ibn ʿIsa connects the story to Jewish injustice and broken covenants, rebuking them, warning that wrongdoing returns on its perpetrators, and consoling the Prophet for their treatment.
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r6.anchor: إن حال اليهود في الظلم ونقض العهد، كحال ابن آدم في ظلمه لأخيه

JISHUMI:v3p1932/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r7.claim: Abu Muslim connects the story to the command to debate the People of the Book from scripture and disclose its hidden reports as proof of the Prophet's truthfulness.
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r7.anchor: عن أسرار ما في كتابهم، شاهدا على صدقه، وهذا من أسرار أحاديثهم عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v3p1932/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r8.claim: The story follows the command to tell them about Adam's sons so they can learn that obedience, disobedience, and their consequences follow the same pattern.
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r8.anchor: اذكر لهم حديث ابني آدم ليعلموا أن سبيلهم في الطاعة والمعصية وعاقبتها كسبيلهم

JISHUMI:v3p1932/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r9.speaker: أبو حامد
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r9.claim: Abu Hamid links the story to the People of the Book claiming to be God's children and beloved: descent from prophets does not save unbelievers, as Adam's son shows.
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r9.anchor: يتصل بقوله: نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه أي: لا ينفعهم كونهم من أولاد الأنبياء مع كفرهم

JISHUMI:v3p1932/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r10.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r10.claim: Al-Asamm says the People of the Book rejected Muhammad out of envy, so the story warns them that envy leads to a bad end.
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r10.anchor: أخبرهم بخبر ابن آدم، وما ناله من الحسد من سوء العاقبة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r1.claim: One account identifies the two sons as Cain and Abel: Adam paired each twin with the other, but Cain envied Abel because his own twin Iqlīmā was more beautiful; fire consumed Abel’s offering, and Cain threatened him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r1.anchor: هما ابنا آدم لصلبه قابيل وهابيل اوحى الله إلى آدم أن يزوج كل واحد منهما توأمه الآخر وكانت توامة قابيل اجمل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r2.claim: Another view says the two men were Israelites, not Adam’s sons.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r2.anchor: وقيل هما رجلان من بني اسرائيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r3.claim: Bi-l-ḥaqq may mean recite an account marked by truth and soundness.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r4.claim: It may mean an accurate account agreeing with the earlier scriptures.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r4.anchor: أو اتله نبأ ملتبسا بالصدق موافقا لما في كتب الأولين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r5.claim: It may refer to the proper aim of condemning envy, since polytheists and the People of the Book envied and opposed the Prophet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r5.anchor: أو بالغرض الصحيح وهو تقبيح الحسد لأن المشركين واهل الكتاب كلهم كانوا يحسدون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r6.claim: Another reading means: tell them the account while being truthful and in the right.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r6.anchor: أو اتل عليهم وانت محق صادق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r7.claim: The time clause may be governed by al-nabaʾ, meaning their story at that time.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r7.anchor: نصب بالنبأ أي قصتهم وحديثهم في ذلك الوقت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, it is apposition to al-nabaʾ, with an omitted annexed noun: ‘the news of that time.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r8.anchor: ويجوز ان يكون بدلا من النبأ أي اتل عليهم النبأ نبأ ذلك الوقت على تقدير حذف المضاف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r9.claim: Qurbān is what one uses to draw near to God, such as a sacrifice or charity, just as ḥulwān is something given.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r9.anchor: والقربان اسم ما يتقرب به إلى الله من نسيكة أو صدقة كما ان الحلوان اسم ما يحلى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r10.speaker: الأصمعي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r10.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī notes that taqarraba is made transitive with bi- to mean qarraba, ‘to bring near.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p657#2/r10.anchor: قال الأصمعي تقربوا قرب القمع فيعدى بالباء حتى يكون بمعنى قرب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r1.claim: Because envy over the accepted offering provoked the death threat, Abel answers that Cain’s failure stems from abandoning piety, not from Abel; he should blame and reform himself.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r1.anchor: لما كان الحسد لأخيه على تقبل قربانه هو الذي حمله على توعده بالقتل قال له إنما أتيت من قبل نفسك لانسلاخها من لباس التقوى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r2.claim: The verse shows that God accepts obedience only from a believing, God-fearing person, a warning to many who perform works.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r2.anchor: وفيه دليل على ان الله تعالى لا يقبل طاعة الا من مؤمن متق فما أنعاه على اكثر العاملين اعمالهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r3.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r3.claim: At death, ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh wept and explained that he heard God say acceptance belongs to the God-fearing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r3.anchor: وعن عامر بن عبد الله انه بكى حين حضرته الوفاة فقيل له ما يبكيك فقد كنت وكنت قال إني أسمع الله يقول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659#2/r3.claim: The tale that Adam stopped laughing for a hundred years and mourned Abel in verse is sheer falsehood; the poem is fabricated and ungrammatical, and prophets are protected from poetry.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659#2/r3.anchor: وروي ان آدم مكث بعد قتله مائة سنة لا يضحك وانه رثاه بشعر وهو كذب بحت وما الشعر الا منحول ملحون وقد صح أن الأنبياء عليهم السلام معصومون من الشعر

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r1.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r1.claim: One view identifies the two sons as Israelites; al-Hasan holds this view.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r1.anchor: فيهما قولان : أحدهما : أنهما من بني إسرائيل , وهذا قول الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Mujahid, and Qatada identify them as Adam's own sons, Abel and Cain.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r2.anchor: والثاني : أنهما ابنا آدم لصلبه , وهما هابيل وقابيل , وهو قول ابن عباس , وابن عمر , ومجاهد , وقتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r3.claim: A qurban is an act of piety intended to seek God's mercy; the word is formed from qurb, nearness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r3.anchor: هو البر الذي يقصد من رحمة الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r4.claim: One view says the brothers offered sacrifices for no particular reason; the better-known account says it arose from a marriage dispute over their twin sisters.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r4.anchor: واختلف في السبب الذي قربا لأجله قربانا على قولين : أحدهما : أنهما فعلاه لغير سبب . والثاني : وهو أشهر القولين

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r5.speaker: قابيل
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r5.claim: In the marriage-dispute account, Cain barred Abel from marrying his twin; one explanation is that Cain claimed priority because he and his twin descended from Paradise while Abel came from earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r5.anchor: أن قابيل قال لهابيل أنا أحق بتوأمتي منك , لأننا من ولادة الجنة وأنت من ولادة الأرض .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r6.claim: Another explanation for Cain's refusal is that his own twin was more beautiful than Abel and Abel's twin.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r6.anchor: الثاني : أنه منعه منها لأن توأمته كانت أحسن من هابيل ومن توأمته

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r7.claim: Abel was a shepherd and offered a choice, fat lamb; Cain was a farmer and offered poor grain. A white fire lifted Abel's offering and left Cain's as the sign of acceptance; there was no poor person to receive alms.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r7.anchor: فقرب هابيل سخلة سمينة من خيار ماله , وقرب قابيل حزمة سنبل من شر ماله , فنزلت نار بيضاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر الطبري
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r8.claim: Al-Tabari says Abel's accepted lamb grazed in Paradise until God used it to ransom Isaac, Abraham's intended sacrifice.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r8.anchor: قال أبو جعفر الطبري : وكانت سخلة هابيل المقبولة ترعى في الجنة حتى فدى الله تعالى بها إحاق بن إبراهيم الذبيح .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r9.claim: Acceptance is explained either by Abel's greater piety, with piety here glossed by exegetes as prayer, or by his offering the best of his property while Cain offered the worst; the latter is attributed to Ibn Umar and most exegetes.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r9.anchor: أحدهما : لأنه كان أتقى لله من قابيل لقوله : { إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين } , والتقوى ها هنا الصلاة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r10.claim: The brothers' offerings were either made at Adam's command after their dispute was referred to him, or were initiated by the brothers themselves.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r10.anchor: واختلف في قربانهما هل كان بأمر آدم , أو من قبل أنفسهما على قولين : أحدهما : أنهما قربا بأمر آدم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r11.claim: Adam went to Mecca to see and visit the House after being commanded to do so; he entrusted Cain with his family's care after the heavens, earth, and mountains refused the trust.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r11.anchor: وكان آدم قد توجه إلى مكة , ليراها ويزور البيت بها عن أمر به , وكان قد عرض الأمانة في حفظ أهله

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r12.claim: On returning, Adam found Cain had killed Abel and the earth had drunk Abel's blood; Adam cursed the earth, which grew thorns and thereafter drank no blood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r12.anchor: ثم توجه وعاد فوجد قابيل قد قتل هابيل وشربت الأرض دمه , فبكى ولعن الأرض لشربها دمه , فأنبتت الشوك

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r13.speaker: علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r13.claim: A report from Ali says Adam mourned Abel in verse; the response says both sons are lost and describes terrible news arriving fearfully.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p27/r13.anchor: روى غياث بن إبراهيم عن أبي إسحاق الهمداني عن علي قال : لما قتل قابيل بن آدم هابيل أخاه بكاه آدم عليه السلام فقال :

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r14.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r14.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Adam's descendants continued marrying sisters for four generations, until a man married his cousin and sibling marriage ended.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r14.anchor: قال ابن جريج : لم يزل بنو آدم فى نكاح الأخوات حتى مضي أربعة آباء , فنكح ابنة عمه وذهب نكاح الأخوات .

MUJAHID:v1p192/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p192/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v1p192/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas relates that Adam had twin male and female children in each of two births; the beautiful sister belonged to the shepherd and the unattractive one to the farmer, who disputed the match and agreed that accepted offerings would decide it.
MUJAHID:v1p192/r1.anchor: عن سعيد ابن جبير عن ابن عباس قال ولد لآدم أربعة تؤم ذكر وأنثى من بطن وذكر وأنثى من بطن فكانت أخت صاحب الحرث جميلة وأخت صاحب الغنم قبيحة

MUJAHID:v1p192/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p192/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v1p192/r2.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbas's account, the shepherd offered a white, horned sheep and the farmer a heap of grain; the sheep was accepted and kept in Paradise for forty years, and was the ram Abraham later sacrificed.
MUJAHID:v1p192/r2.anchor: فجاء صاحب الغنم بكبش أعين أبيض أقرن وجاء صاحب الحرث بصبرة من طعام فقبل الكبش فخزنه الله في الجنة أربعين خريفا

MUJAHID:v1p192/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p192/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v1p192/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas's report concludes that the farmer killed his brother and that all Adam's descendants came from that unbelieving son.
MUJAHID:v1p192/r3.anchor: فقتله صاحب الحرث فولد آدم كلهم من ولد ذلك الكافر

MUJAHID:v1p192/r4.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p192/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v1p192/r4.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbas says Adam was ordered to marry each female twin to a male from the other birth.
MUJAHID:v1p192/r4.anchor: عن علي بن زيد بن جدعان عن يوسف بن مهران عن ابن عباس قال أمر آدم أن يزوج أنثى هذا البطن من ذكر ذاك البطن

MUJAHID:v1p192/r5.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p192/r5.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p192/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies Adam's sons as Abel and Cain: Abel offered a sheep, Cain vegetables, and Abel's offering was accepted while Cain's was rejected.
MUJAHID:v1p192/r5.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ إذ قربا قربانا ﴾ قال هما ابنا آدم لصلبه هابيل وقابيل قرب هابيل شاة وقابيل بقلا

MUJAHID:v1p192/r9.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p192/r9.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p192/r9.claim: Mujahid links the killing to the likeness in 5:32 and to the warning in 4:93 about intentionally killing a believer.
MUJAHID:v1p192/r9.anchor: يقول الله عز وجل ﴿ من قتل نفسا بغير نفس أو فساد في الأرض فكأنما قتل الناس جميعا ﴾ قال هذا مثل قوله ﴿ ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا فجزاؤه جهنم خالدا فيها ﴾

MUQATIL:5:27/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:27/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:27/r1.claim: The Prophet is to recount to the people of Mecca the true story of Habil and Qabil so they recognize his prophethood.
MUQATIL:5:27/r1.anchor: يقول: اتل يا محمد على أهل مكة نبأ ابنى آدم، { بالحق } ليعرفوا نبوتك

MUQATIL:5:27/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:27/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:27/r2.claim: Hawwa bore paired children twice: Qabil with Iqlima, then Habil with Liuda; Qabil's twin sister was more beautiful.
MUQATIL:5:27/r2.anchor: وذلك أن حواء ولدت فى بطن واحد غلاما وجارية، قابيل وإقليما، ثم ولدت فى البطن الآخر غلاما وجارية، هابيل وليوذا

MUQATIL:5:27/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:27/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:27/r3.claim: Adam proposed that each brother marry the other's twin; Qabil objected and wanted to marry his own twin, so Adam made acceptance of an offering decide who deserved her.
MUQATIL:5:27/r3.anchor: قال آدم، عليه السلام، ليتزوج كل واحد منهما أخت الآخر، قال قابيل: لكن يتزوج كل واحد منهما أخته التى ولدت معه

MUQATIL:5:27/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:27/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:27/r4.claim: Qabil, a farmer, offered his worst grain, mixed with darnel; Habil, a herdsman, offered his best sheep with butter and milk.
MUQATIL:5:27/r4.anchor: فعمد قابيل، وكان صاحب زرع، فقرب أخبث زرعه البر المأكول فيه الزوان، وكان هابيل صاحب ماشية، فعمد فقرب خير غنمه مع زبد ولبن

MUQATIL:5:27/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:27/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:27/r5.claim: After the brothers prayed at the offering place, a fire descended from heaven and consumed Habil's offering, leaving Qabil's untouched.
MUQATIL:5:27/r5.anchor: فنزلت نار من السماء، فأكلت قربان هابيل، وتركت قربان قابيل، فحسده قابيل، فقال لهابيل: لأقتلنك

MUQATIL:5:27/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:27/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:27/r6.claim: Jealous Qabil threatened Habil; Habil urged him not to stain his hands with innocent blood and warned that murder would bring misery, fear, and God's curse.
MUQATIL:5:27/r6.anchor: فحسده قابيل، فقال لهابيل: لأقتلنك، قال هابيل: يا أخى، لا تلطخ يدك بدم برئ

MUQATIL:5:27/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:27/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:27/r7.claim: In their conversation through midday, Habil said that if Qabil killed him, Qabil would be the first of their father's descendants condemned to misery and led to the Fire, while Habil would be the first martyr to enter Paradise.
MUQATIL:5:27/r7.anchor: إن أنت قتلتنى كنت أول من كتب عليه الشقاء، وأول من يساق إلى النار من ذرية والدى، وكنت أنا أول شهيد يدخل الجنة

MUQATIL:5:27/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:27/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:27/r8.claim: Qabil complained that Habil's offering had been accepted while his was rejected; Habil said this meant Qabil would suffer forever, and Qabil killed him with a stone that crushed his head in India at evening while Adam was in Mecca.
MUQATIL:5:27/r8.anchor: ويقال: قد تقبل قربانه ولم يتقبل قربانى، فقال له هابيل: فتشقى آخر الأبد، فغضب عند ذلك قابيل

MUQATIL:5:27/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:27/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:27/r9.claim: Qabil killed Habil with a stone that crushed his head in India at evening, while Adam was in Mecca.
MUQATIL:5:27/r9.anchor: فقتله بحجر دق رأسه، وذلك بأرض الهند عشية، وآدم، عليه السلام، بمكة

MUQATIL:5:27/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:27/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:27/r10.claim: God accepts an offering only from those who fear Him.
MUQATIL:5:27/r10.anchor: قال إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r1.claim: God commands Muhammad to tell those who envy him what envy caused, so they will desist and believe his message.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r1.anchor: أمر الله تعالى مححد صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يقص على حاسديه ما جرى بسبب الحسد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r2.claim: The people to be told are the People of the Book.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r3.claim: The two sons may be Hābīl and Qābīl from Adam’s descendants, or two Israelite men.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r3.anchor: ومن صلبه هابيل وقابيل أو هما رجلان من بنى إسرائيل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r4.claim: «In truth» may mean an account agreeing with earlier scriptures, a truthful and sound telling, or that Muhammad tells it truthfully.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r4.anchor: بالصدق موافقا لما فى كتب الأولين أو تلاوة ملتبسة بالصدق والصحة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r5.claim: «When they offered» is governed by «the account» as their story then, or is in apposition with an omitted genitive.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r5.anchor: نصب بالنبأ أى قصتهما وحديثهما فى ذلك الوقت أو بدل من النبأ

NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r6.claim: Qurbān is an offering to draw near to God, whether sacrifice or charity; each brother brought his own offering.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r6.anchor: ما يتقرب به إلى الله من نسيكة أو صدقة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r7.claim: The account says God told Adam to marry each son to the other’s twin; Qābīl envied Hābīl over the more beautiful Iqlīmā, so Adam ordered offerings and fire consumed Hābīl’s.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r7.anchor: روى أنه اوحى الله تعالى إلى آدم أن يزوج كل واحد منهما توأمه الآخر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r8.claim: After Hābīl’s offering was accepted, Qābīl’s jealousy and anger grew and he threatened murder.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r8.anchor: فازداد قابيل حسدا وسخطا وتوعده بالقتل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r9.claim: Hābīl means that God accepts only from the pious; Qābīl was not pious, so rejection was due to his own lack of piety, not his brother.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r9.anchor: فإنما أوتيت من قبل نفسك لانسلاخها من لباس التقوى لا من قبلى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r10.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r10.claim: ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh wept near death; asked why, he said he heard God say that He accepts only from the pious.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p278#3/r10.anchor: وعن عامر بن عبد الله أنه بكى حين حضرته الوفاة

BURSEVI:v2p303/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p303/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p303/r1.claim: A report says Joshua asked Moses in a dream how death felt; Moses likened it to being skinned alive. Moses lived 120 years, and after his death and forty years God sent Joshua as prophet to fight the giants.
BURSEVI:v2p303/r1.anchor: وكان عمر موسى مائة وعشرين سنة فلما مات موسى وانقضت الأربعون بعث الله يوشع نبيا

BURSEVI:v2p303/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p303/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p303/r2.claim: Joshua led the Israelites to Jericho with the Ark; after six months' siege they sounded horns and shouted together, the wall fell, and they defeated the giants.
BURSEVI:v2p303/r2.anchor: معه تابوت الميثاق فأحاط بمدينة أريحاء ستة أشهر

BURSEVI:v2p303/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p303/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p303/r3.claim: When sunset approached on Friday and the Sabbath was near, Joshua prayed for more daylight; the sun stopped and the day was lengthened so he could finish the battle, after which he conquered thirty-one Syrian kings and all Syria.
BURSEVI:v2p303/r3.anchor: وكان القتال يوم الجمعة فبقيت منهم البقية وكادت الشمس تغرب وتدخل ليلة السبت فقال : اللهم اردد الشمس علي

BURSEVI:v2p303/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p303/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p303/r4.claim: The collected spoils did not burn until a thief was identified by an allegiance test; he produced a jeweled golden bull's head, which was placed in the offering, and fire consumed both it and him.
BURSEVI:v2p303/r4.anchor: وجمع الغنائم فلم تنزل النار فأوحى الله إلى يوشع أن فيها غلولا فمرهم فليبايعوك فبايعوه فالتصقت يد رجل منهم بيده

BURSEVI:v2p303/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p303/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p303/r5.claim: The account says Joshua was buried on Mount Ephraim at age 126 after directing Israel for twenty-seven years.
BURSEVI:v2p303/r5.anchor: ثم مات يوشع ودفن في جبل افرائيم وكان عمره مائة وستا وعشرين سنة وتدبيره أمر بني إسرائيل بعد موت موسى سبعا وعشرين سنة

BURSEVI:v2p303/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p303/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p303/r6.claim: A Persian couplet accompanying the account says the world will remain with no one, so the heart should attach only to the Creator of the world.
BURSEVI:v2p303/r6.anchor: جهان أي بردار نماند بكس دل اندر جهان آفرين بندوبس

BURSEVI:v2p303/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p303/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p303/r7.claim: The command is to recite to the People of Scripture the true and accurate account of Adam's two sons, Cain and Abel.
BURSEVI:v2p303/r7.anchor: {نبأ ابنى ءادم} أي : خبر ابني أبي البشر وهما قابيل وهابيل

BURSEVI:v2p303/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p303/r8.speaker: العلماء
BURSEVI:v2p303/r8.claim: Scholars say Eve bore twins, boy and girl, in each pregnancy except Seth's; Adam was told to marry each son to the other's twin because there were no other women.
BURSEVI:v2p303/r8.anchor: ذكر العلماء أن حواء كانت تلد في كل بطن ولدين ذكرا وأنثى الاشيثا فإنها ولدته منفردا فولدت أول بطن قابيل وأخته اقليما

BURSEVI:v2p303/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p303/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p303/r9.claim: Cain's twin was more beautiful, so he envied Abel, resented what he thought was Adam's decision, and demanded that both offer sacrifices, with the accepted offering deciding who married her.
BURSEVI:v2p303/r9.anchor: وكانت توأمة قابيل أجمل فحسد عليها أخاه وسخط وزعم أن ذلك ليس من عند الله بل من جهة آدم فقال لهما قربا قربانا

BURSEVI:v2p303/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p303/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p303/r10.claim: Qurban means something by which one seeks nearness to God, such as an animal sacrifice or charity; it is singular because it began as a verbal noun, with each brother bringing one understood.
BURSEVI:v2p303/r10.anchor: والقربان اسم لما يتقرب به إلى الله تعالى من ذبيحة أو صدقة وتوحيده لما أنه في الأصل مصدر والتقدير إذ قرب كل منهما قربانا

BURSEVI:v2p303/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p303/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p303/r11.claim: Abel, who raised livestock, brought a fine camel or ram with milk and butter; after Adam prayed, a smokeless white fire descended from heaven and consumed it.
BURSEVI:v2p303/r11.anchor: هو هابيل وكان صاحب ضرع وقرب جملا سمينا أو كبشا ولبنا وزبدا فنزلت نار من السماء بيضاء لا دخان لها فأكلته

BURSEVI:v2p303/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p303/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p303/r12.claim: In that era, a heavenly fire consuming an offering marked its acceptance; when an offering was not accepted, the fire did not descend and birds or beasts ate it. Another explanation is that there were then no poor recipients for charity.
BURSEVI:v2p303/r12.anchor: وكانت القرابين إذا كانت مقبولة نزلت من السماء نار فأكلتها وإن لم تكن مقبولة لم تنزل النار وأكلتها الطير والسباع

BURSEVI:v2p304/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p304/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BURSEVI:v2p304/r1.claim: Sa'id b. Jubayr and others report that fire from heaven carried Abel's offering up to Paradise, where it remained until it was used to ransom the one sacrificed.
BURSEVI:v2p304/r1.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير وغيره نزلت نار من السماء فاحتملت قربان هابيل ورفع بها إلى الجنة فلم يزل يرعى

BURSEVI:v2p304/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p304/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p304/r2.claim: Cain farmed crops and offered the worst wheat; fire did not touch it because he resented God's judgment, lacked sincere intent, and deliberately offered his poorest produce.
BURSEVI:v2p304/r2.anchor: وهو قابيل كان صاحب زرع وقرب اردأ ما عنده من القمح ولم تتعرض له النار أصلا لأنه سخط حكم الله ولم يخلص النية

BURSEVI:v2p304/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p304/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p304/r3.claim: After the rejected offering, Cain's jealousy grew while Adam was away in Mecca; he threatened Abel because God had accepted Abel's sacrifice, Abel would marry the beautiful sister, and Abel's descendants might boast over his.
BURSEVI:v2p304/r3.anchor: وقد غضب قابيل لرد قربانه وكان يضمر الحسد في نفسه إلى أن أتى آدم مكة لزيارة البيت فلما غاب آدم أتيى قابيل هابيل

BURSEVI:v2p304/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p304/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p304/r4.claim: Cain's stated reasons for murder were that God accepted Abel's sacrifice, Abel would marry the prettier sister, and people would say Abel was better and his descendants would boast over Cain.
BURSEVI:v2p304/r4.anchor: قال : ولم قال لأن الله قبل قربانك

BURSEVI:v2p304/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p304/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p304/r5.claim: Abel says God accepts offerings only from the God-fearing; the different outcomes reflect their piety, so Cain's failure comes from himself, not Abel.
BURSEVI:v2p304/r5.anchor: {إنما يتقبل الله} أي : القربان {من المتقين} لا من غيرهم وإنما تقبل قرباني ورد قربانك

BURSEVI:v2p304/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p304/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p304/r6.claim: The author cites the Prophet's gesture to his heart as an explanation of where piety resides.
BURSEVI:v2p304/r6.anchor: والتقوى من صفات القلب لقوله عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v2p304/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p304/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p304/r7.claim: True piety means acting with fear that one's worship is deficient, carefully avoiding worship for any purpose besides God's pleasure, and excluding any partner from it.
BURSEVI:v2p304/r7.anchor: وحقيقة التقوى أن يكون العامل على خوف ووجل من تقصير نفسه فيما أتى به من الطاعات وأن يكون في غاية الاحتراز من أن يأتي بتلك الطاعة لغرض سوى طلب مرضاة الله

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r1.claim: The story links to the preceding passage by likening Jewish oppression and broken covenants to the first brother’s violence; it warns, rebukes Islam’s opponents, and consoles the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r1.anchor: وجه اتصال هذه الآية بما قبلها التنبيه من الله تعالى على أن ظلم اليهود، ونقضهم المواثيق والعهود كظلم ابن آدم لأخيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r2.claim: If the Jews plotted to kill Muhammad, they would repeat an old evil: earlier prophets were killed, as Cain killed Abel; this is a truthful account, not fabricated tales.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r2.anchor: إن هم هؤلاء اليهود بالفتك بك يا محمد فقد قتلوا قبلك الأنبياء، وقتل قابيل هابيل، والشر قديم.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r3.speaker: الحسن البصري
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī says they were not Adam’s biological sons, but Israelites used as a parable to expose Jewish envy; he says sacrifices existed only among Israelites.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r3.anchor: فقال الحسن البصري: ليسا لصلبه، كانا رجلين من بني إسرائيل ضرب الله بهما المثل في إبانة حسد اليهود

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls al-Ḥasan’s account mistaken: how could an Israelite not know burial and need a crow to teach it?
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا وهم، وكيف يجهل صورة الدفن أحد من بني إسرائيل حتى يقتدي بالغراب؟

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r5.speaker: الجمهور من المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r5.claim: The author prefers the majority view that these were Adam’s own sons, Cain and Abel; Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿUmar also held this.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r5.anchor: والصحيح أنهما ابناه لصلبه هذا قول الجمهور من المفسرين وقاله ابن عباس وابن عمر وغيرهما

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r6.claim: Cain, a farmer, offered an inferior bundle of grain, finding and eating a good stalk among it; Abel, a shepherd, offered his best ram.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r6.anchor: وكان قربان قابيل حزمة من سنبل لأنه كان صاحب زرع واختارها من أردإ زرعه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r7.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and others say Abel’s accepted ram was raised to Paradise and remained there until it was offered as the ransom of the one to be sacrificed.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r7.anchor: فرفع إلى الجنة، فلم يزل يرعى فيها إلى أن فدي به الذبيح عليه السلام قاله سعيد بن جبير وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r8.claim: Cain, an unbeliever, resented that Abel’s offering was accepted because Abel was a believer, and threatened to kill him out of envy.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r8.anchor: فلما تقبل قربان هابيل لأنه كان مؤمنا قال له قابيل حسدا: لأنه كان كافرا

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r9.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين منهم ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r9.claim: A reported account says Eve bore twins in each pregnancy except Seth; Cain demanded his beautiful twin, disobeyed Adam’s cross-pregnancy marriage order, and the brothers agreed to offer sacrifices. Adam was reportedly present.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r9.anchor: وكان يزوج الذكر من هذا البطن الأنثى من البطن الآخر، ولا تحل له أخته توءمته فولدت مع قابيل أختا جميلة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r10.speaker: جعفر الصادق
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r10.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq’s alternative account rejects sibling marriage and pairs Cain with a jinn woman and Abel with a heavenly maiden.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r10.anchor: وقد روي في هذا الباب عن جعفر الصادق: أن آدم لم يكن يزوج ابنته من ابنه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r11.claim: In Jaʿfar’s account, Eve’s daughter ʿAnāq was the first to transgress on earth, and God had her killed before Cain and Abel were born.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r11.anchor: وجمع بينهما ولدت حواء بنتا فسماها عناقا

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r12.claim: Jaʿfar’s account says God paired Cain with a jinn woman named Jamāla, then sent Abel a heavenly maiden named Bazla and created a womb for her.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27/r12.anchor: وأوحى الله لآدم أن زوجها من قابيل فزوجها منه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r1.claim: In Jaʿfar’s account, Cain objects that he is older and deserved the match; Adam says God commanded it and proposes the accepted offering settle the dispute.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r1.anchor: فقال قابيل: يا أبت ألست أكبر من أخي؟ قال: نعم. قال: فكنت أحق بما فعلت به منه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r2.claim: The author doubts Jaʿfar’s story and prefers cross-pregnancy marriage; he cites 4:1 as near-explicit evidence and says the arrangement was later abrogated.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r2.anchor: قلت: هذه القصة عن جعفر ما أظنها تصح، وأن القول ما ذكرناه من أنه كان يزوج غلام هذا البطن لجارية تلك البطن.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r3.claim: The author cites 4:1 as nearly explicit evidence for the common-parent account; the sibling-marriage arrangement was later abrogated as discussed in al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r3.anchor: والدليل على هذا من الكتاب قوله تعالى: ياأيها الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r4.claim: The account says Eve bore forty children, male and female, in twenty pregnancies, beginning with Cain and Iqlīmiyāʾ and ending with ʿAbd al-Mughīth; Ibn ʿAbbās says Adam saw forty thousand descendants.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r4.anchor: وكان جميع ما ولدته حواء أربعين من ذكر وأنثى في عشرين بطنا أولهم قابيل وتوءمته إقليمياء

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r5.claim: The author rejects the report that Adam’s daughter fornicated, asking with whom she could have done so; such a claim requires sound transmission, which is absent.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r5.anchor: وما روى عن جعفر من قوله: فولدت بنتا وأنها بغت فيقال: مع من بغت؟

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r6.claim: Abel’s omitted response is reconstructed: Cain has no grounds to kill him over the accepted offering, since Abel acted righteously and God accepts only from the God-fearing.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r6.anchor: قال له: ولم تقتلني وأنا لم أجن شيئا؟، ولا ذنب لي في قبول الله قرباني

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says piety here means avoiding associationism, by Sunni consensus; sincere deeds of a monotheist are accepted, while avoiding sins brings the highest acceptance, known by revelation rather than rational obligation.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطية: المراد بالتقوى هنا اتقاء الشرك بإجماع أهل السنة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r8.speaker: عدي بن ثابت وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r8.claim: ʿAdī ibn Thābit and others say the sacrifice of this community is prayer; the author says this applies specifically to one kind of worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#2/r8.anchor: وقال عدي بن ثابت وغيره: قربان متقي هذه الأمة الصلاة. قلت: وهذا خاص في نوع من العبادات.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#3/r1.claim: A report al-Bukhārī transmits from Abū Hurayra says God declares war on one who harms a devoted servant; obligatory acts are most beloved, then supererogatory acts draw the servant near until God loves him, answers requests, and protects him.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:27#3/r1.anchor: إن الله تبارك وتعالى قال من عادى لي وليا فقد آذنته بالحرب

RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r1.claim: The story follows the reminder that God protected believers from enemies (5:11) and consoles Muhammad: people have always envied those given great blessings, as the successive stories show.
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r1.anchor: فذكر تعالى أن الأعداء يريدون إيقاع البلاء والمحنة بهم لكنه تعالى يحفظهم بفضله

RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r2.claim: Another proposed link is to the passage cited as 5:15: this story and the law of retaliation it illustrates are among the Torah's concealed matters.
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r2.anchor: وهذه القصة وكيفية إيجاب القصاص عليها من أسرار التوراة

RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r3.claim: The story may continue the account of Moses and the giants; it teaches the Jews that their ancestors' regret after sin resembled the regret in Adam's sons' story.
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r3.anchor: القصة متعلقة بما قبلها ، وهي قصة محاربة الجبارين

RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r4.claim: It may connect to the claim “we are God's children and beloved”: descent from a revered prophet does not save unbelieving descendants, as Adam's son gained nothing from his father's standing.
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r4.anchor: أي لا ينفعهم كونهم من أولاد الأنبياء مع كفرهم

RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r5.claim: Since the People of the Book envied Muhammad and rejected him, the story warns them that envy brought its perpetrator to a disastrous end.
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#2/r5.anchor: لما كفر أهل الكتاب بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم حسدا أخبرهم الله تعالى بخبر ابن آدم

RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r1.claim: The command “recite to them” is read either as addressing people generally or specifically the People of the Book.
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r1.anchor: فيه قولان : أحدهما : واتل على الناس

RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r2.claim: The first view identifies the two as Adam's biological sons, Abel and Cain.
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r2.anchor: الأول : أنهما ابنا آدم من صلبه ، وهما هابيل وقابيل

RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r3.claim: One account says Abel was a shepherd and offered his best sheep, while Cain offered inferior grain; heavenly fire accepted Abel's offering, prompting Cain's envy and murderous intent.
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r3.anchor: أن هابيل كان صاحب غنم ، وقابيل كان صاحب زرع

RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r4.claim: Another account says Adam had male-female twins and arranged cross-marriages; Cain refused to let his more beautiful twin sister marry Abel, and after their offerings were made the accepted offering led Cain to kill Abel out of envy.
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r4.anchor: ما روي أن آدم عليه السلام كان يولد له في كل بطن غلام وجارية وكان يزوج البنت من بطن الغلام من بطن آخر

RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r5.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r5.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak say the two men were Israelites, not Adam's biological sons; the Israelite law of retaliation in 5:32 makes better sense if the crime occurred among Israelites.
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r5.anchor: والقول الثاني : وهو قول الحسن والضحاك

RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r6.claim: The Israelite reading argues that the story's purpose is to expose the Jews' ancient, extreme envy: even seeing a God-accepted offering failed to make the envied man honor its recipient.
RAZI-FULL:v11p160#3/r6.anchor: وإذا كان المراد من ذكر هذه القصة بيان أن الحسد دأب قديم في بني إسرائيل

RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r1.claim: Razi prefers that these were Adam's own sons: Cain's ignorance of how to bury Abel until he saw the crow would be implausible if he were an Israelite.
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r1.anchor: واعلم أن القول الأول هو الذي اختاره أكثر أصحاب الأخبار

RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r2.claim: One reading means the recitation is true and sound, coming from God.
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r2.anchor: بالحق ، أي تلاوة متلبسة بالحق والصحة من عند الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r3.claim: Another reading means the recitation is truthful and agrees with what is in the Torah and Gospel.
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r3.anchor: أي تلاوة متلبسة بالصدق والحق موافقة لما في التوراة والإنجيل

RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r4.claim: A third reading takes “in truth” to mean with the proper purpose of condemning envy, which the idolaters and People of the Book showed toward Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r4.anchor: بالحق ، أي بالغرض الصحيح وهو تقبيح الحسد

RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r5.claim: The story is recited for moral reflection, not idle entertainment; Razi links this lesson to the statement that earlier stories contain a lesson for people of understanding.
RAZI-FULL:v11p161/r5.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن المقصود بالذكر من الأقاصيص والقصص في القرآن العبرة

RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r1.claim: Most exegetes say acceptance was signaled when fire consumed the offering; Razi prefers this account because most commentators agree on it.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r1.anchor: قيل : كانت علامة القبول أن تأكله النار وهو قول أكثر المفسرين

RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r2.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r2.claim: Mujahid reverses the sign, saying that fire consuming the offering marked its rejection; Razi favors the majority view instead.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد : علامة الرد أن تأكله النار

RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r3.claim: A further account says there were no poor people then to receive offerings, so fire descended from heaven and consumed them.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r3.anchor: وقيل : ما كان في ذلك الوقت فقير يدفع إليه

RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r4.claim: Piety is a condition for accepting deeds: as 22:37 says, what reaches God is not sacrificial meat or blood but the piety within people.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r4.anchor: إنما صار القربانين مقبولا والآخر مردودا لأن حصول التقوى شرط في قبول الأعمال

RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r5.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r5.claim: The Prophet pointed to his heart when saying that piety is here, locating piety in the heart.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r5.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( التقوى هاهنا ) وأشار إلى القلب

RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r6.claim: True piety includes fearing one's own shortcomings in worship, seeking only God's pleasure in worship, and guarding against associating anything else with God; observing these conditions is difficult.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r6.anchor: وحقيقة التقوى أمور : أحدها : أن يكون على خوف

RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r7.claim: One account explains the different outcomes by saying one brother offered his best possession and the other his worst.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r7.anchor: وقيل في هذه القصة : إن أحدهما جعل قربانه أحسن

RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r8.claim: Another explanation says Cain did not care whether his offering was accepted and would not give his sister in marriage to Abel.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r8.anchor: وقيل : إنه أضمر أنه لا يبالي سواء قبل أو لم يقبل

RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r9.claim: A further explanation is that Cain was not pious or obedient, which is why God did not accept his offering.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r9.anchor: وقيل : كان قابيل ليس من أهل التقوى والطاعة

RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r10.claim: Razi supplies the omitted exchange: Cain asks why he should not kill Abel, explains that Abel's offering was accepted, and Abel replies that acceptance depends on piety, not on Abel's wrongdoing.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r10.anchor: لم تقتلني ؟ قال لأن قربانك صار مقبولا

RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r11.claim: Alternatively, the statement about God accepting only the pious is a divine parenthetical address to Muhammad, explaining that Cain's offering was rejected because he lacked piety.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162/r11.anchor: وقيل : هذا من كلام الله تعالى لنبيه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r3.claim: يقبل is used of a person receiving prayer or alms in this life, while يتقبل is used of God accepting or not accepting deeds in the afterlife.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p596/r3.anchor: (يقبل) من الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يقبل الصلاة والزكاة

RAZI-FULL:v22p31#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p31#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p31#2/r3.claim: Unlike ordinary stories, whose retelling Muhammad is commanded to deliver, the prayer answer omits qul to show that no intermediary stands between God and the supplicant; God speaks directly.
RAZI-FULL:v22p31#2/r3.anchor: والحاصل كأنه سبحانه وتعالى قال : يا محمد إذا سئلت عن غيري فكن أنت المجيب
